akhfash:9-10.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا عَلِمَ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا شَيْئاً﴾ and then said ﴿مِّن وَرَآئِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلاَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُم مَّا كَسَبُواْ شَيْئاً﴾: He used the plural because He had said ﴿وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ﴾ [7], which has the meaning of a group, like the things that come in singular form while their meaning is plural. He has also made ﴿الذي﴾ equivalent to ﴿من﴾, saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾: "الذي" is singular in form, then He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.

akhfash:21-21.t: And He said ﴿سَوَآءٌ مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾ in the nominative. Some said: the living and the dying belong to the disbelievers, as though He said: "Or do those who have committed evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds?" Then He said "equal are the living of the disbelievers and their dying", i.e. their living is an evil living and their dying an evil dying; so he put "السواء" in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Whoever explains "the living" and "the dying" as belonging to the disbelievers and the believers may, in this meaning, have "السواء" in the accusative or the nominative: whoever makes "السواء" mean "equal" (مستويا) should put it in the nominative because it is the noun (subject), unless he puts "the living" and "the dying" in the accusative as a badal (substitute) and "السواء" in the accusative (as ḥāl) meaning "being equal". And if he wishes he puts "السواء" in the nominative when it has the meaning of "equal", because it is an attribute that is not inflected (like a verb), just as you say "رأيتْ رَجُلاً خيراً منهُ أَبُوهُ" (I saw a man whose father is better than he). The nominative is better.

akhfash:31-31.t: [And] He said ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, i.e. it will be said to them: "Were My verses not recited to you?" The fāʾ came in because of "أمّا".

akhfash:32-32.t: And He said ﴿إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلاَّ ظَنّاً﴾: we think nothing but conjecture.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿هَذَا كِتَابُنَا﴾ the register of the recording angels (al-ḥafaẓa) ﴿يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ﴾ We were recording and preserving ﴿مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ His Garden ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear, the manifest.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ it will be said to them: ﴿أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي﴾ the Quran ﴿تُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ you were arrogant ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ disbelievers.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ﴾ to you, O disbelievers, ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of the resurrection ﴿حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ﴾ with the nominative (rafʿ) and the accusative (naṣb) ﴿لَا رَيْبَ﴾ no doubt ﴿فِيهَا قُلْتُمْ مَا نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ إِنْ﴾ i.e. «مَا» (not) ﴿نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا﴾ al-Mubarrad said: its underlying form is «إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا نَظُنُّ ظَنًّا» ("we are nothing but conjecturing a conjecture") ﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ﴾ that it is coming.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَبَدَا﴾ appeared ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿سَيِّئَاتُ مَا عَمِلُوا﴾ in this world, i.e. their recompense ﴿وَحَاقَ﴾ descended ﴿بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ i.e. the punishment.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنْسَاكُمْ﴾ We leave you in the Fire ﴿كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَذَا﴾ i.e. you abandoned working for its meeting ﴿وَمَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾ who could protect you from it.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ بِأَنَّكُمُ اتَّخَذْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿هُزُوًا وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ until you said: there is no resurrection and no reckoning ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ لَا يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ in the active voice and in the passive [يُخْرَجُونَ] ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ from the Fire ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ i.e. they will not be asked to make their Lord pleased through repentance and obedience, because that will be of no benefit on that Day.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ﴾ praise, i.e. describing with beauty, for His fulfilling His promise concerning the deniers ﴿رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ i.e. the Creator of what has been mentioned. The ʿālam (world) is everything other than Allah; it is put in the plural because of the diversity of its kinds. And «رَبِّ» is a badal (substitute).

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ﴾ grandeur ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being in them ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ this has preceded.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿حم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran; mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate) ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمِ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. in their creation ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ pointing to the power and Oneness of Allah the Exalted ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ﴾ i.e. in the creation of each of you from a sperm-drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, until he becomes a human being ﴿وَ﴾ the creation of ﴿مَا يَبُثُّ﴾ He scatters on the earth ﴿مِنْ دَابَّةٍ﴾ which is whatever creeps upon the earth, people and others ﴿آيَاتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ in the Resurrection.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَ﴾ in ﴿اخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ﴾ their going and coming ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ رِزْقٍ﴾ rain, because it is the cause of provision ﴿فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ﴾ turning them, now south and now north, cold and hot ﴿آيَاتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the proof, and so believe.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ the aforementioned signs ﴿آيَاتُ اللَّهِ﴾ His proofs pointing to His Oneness ﴿نَتْلُوهَا﴾ We narrate them ﴿عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) نَتْلُو ﴿فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. His discourse, which is the Quran ﴿وَآيَاتِهِ﴾ His proofs ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca; i.e. they will not believe. And in one reading with tāʾ.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ a word of punishment ﴿لِكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ﴾ great liar ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ of much sin.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَسْمَعُ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ﴾ on his disbelief ﴿مُسْتَكْبِرًا﴾ arrogant towards faith ﴿كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْهَا فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَإِذَا عَلِمَ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿شَيْئًا اتَّخَذَهَا هُزُوًا﴾ i.e. something mocked ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ i.e. the great liars ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ involving humiliation.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ﴾ i.e. in front of them, because they are in this world ﴿جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مَا كَسَبُوا﴾ of wealth and deeds ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَا مَا اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the idols ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿هُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ﴾ a portion ﴿مِنْ رِجْزٍ﴾ i.e. punishment ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْبَحْرَ لِتَجْرِيَ الْفُلْكُ﴾ the ships ﴿فِيهِ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ by His permission ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ seek, through trade ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ of sun, moon, stars, water and other things ﴿وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ of beasts, trees, plants, rivers and other things, i.e. He created that for your benefit ﴿جَمِيعًا﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He subjected them as being from Him, the Exalted ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ about them, and so believe.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ fear ﴿أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ﴾ His decisive events, i.e. forgive the disbelievers the harm that came from them to you; and this was before the command to wage jihad against them ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ i.e. Allah; and in one reading with nūn ﴿قَوْمًا بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ of forgiving the disbelievers their harm.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ﴾ he works ﴿وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فَعَلَيْهَا﴾ he does evil ﴿ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ you will end up, and He will recompense the one who does right and the one who does evil.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿وَالْحُكْمَ﴾ by it among people ﴿وَالنُّبُوَّةَ﴾ for Mūsā and Hārūn among them ﴿وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ the lawful things, such as the manna and the quails ﴿وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the rational beings of their time.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُمْ بَيِّنَاتٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ the matter of religion: the lawful and the unlawful, and the sending of Muhammad, upon him be the best of blessings and peace ﴿فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ about his being sent ﴿إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ i.e. because of a transgression that arose among them, out of envy of him ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿عَلَى شَرِيعَةٍ﴾ a way ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ the matter of religion ﴿فَاتَّبِعْهَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ in the worship of other than Allah.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يُغْنُوا﴾ ward off ﴿عَنْكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ of His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the believers.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ the Quran ﴿بَصَائِرُ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ landmarks by which they gain insight into the rulings and the ḥadd limits ﴿وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ in the Resurrection.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ in the meaning of the hamza of denial ﴿حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا﴾ earned ﴿السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ disbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَاءً﴾ a khabar (predicate) [and in one reading سَوَاءٌ] ﴿مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a maʿṭūf (conjoined); and the clause is a badal (substitute) for the kāf; and the two pronouns refer to the disbelievers. The meaning: do they suppose that We will place them in the Hereafter in good, like the believers, in an easy life equal to their life in this world, since they said to the believers: "If we are resurrected, we will be given of good the like of what you are given"? The Exalted said, in accordance with His denial by means of the hamza: ﴿سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾ i.e. the matter is not so; rather they will be in the Hereafter in punishment, contrary to their life in this world, and the believers will be in the Hereafter in reward, for their doing righteous deeds in this world — prayer, zakat, fasting and so on. And مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), i.e. evil as a judgement is this judgement of theirs.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَ﴾ created ﴿الْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) خَلَقَ, so as to point to His power and Oneness ﴿وَلِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ of acts of disobedience and of obedience, so the disbeliever is not equal to the believer ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ﴾ tell me ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾ whatever he fancies, one stone after another that he considers finer ﴿وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ﴾ on His part, the Exalted, i.e. knowing that he was among the people of misguidance before creating him ﴿وَخَتَمَ عَلَى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ﴾ so he did not hear guidance nor understand it ﴿وَجَعَلَ عَلَى بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً﴾ darkness, so he did not see guidance. Here the second object of رَأَيْتَ is implied: "will he be guided?" ﴿فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. after His leading him astray; i.e. he will not be guided ﴿أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ take heed; in it is the assimilation (idghām) of one of the two tāʾs into the dhāl [تَذَكَّرُونَ].

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ i.e. those who deny the Resurrection ﴿مَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. life ﴿إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا﴾ which is in ﴿الدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا﴾ i.e. some die and some live, by being born ﴿وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ﴾ i.e. the passing of time. The Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ﴾ statement ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ﴾ i.e. مَا (not) ﴿هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا﴾ of the Quran, pointing to Our power to resurrect ﴿بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ clear; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿مَا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا ائْتُوا بِآبَائِنَا﴾ alive ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that we will be resurrected.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾ when you were sperm-drops ﴿ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ﴾ alive ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ لَا رَيْبَ﴾ no doubt ﴿فِيهِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are those who say what was mentioned ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ﴾ from which is substituted (badal) ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ the disbelievers, i.e. their loss becomes manifest, in that they end up in the Fire.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَتَرَى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ﴾ i.e. the people of a religion ﴿جَاثِيَةً﴾ on their knees, or gathered together ﴿كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعَى إِلَى كِتَابِهَا﴾ the book of its deeds; and it will be said to them: ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ i.e. its recompense.

daas-irab:31-33.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded in the previous verse. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle of affirmation (taqrīr), the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted, and lam is a particle of jussive (jazm). ﴿تَكُنْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam. ﴿آياتِي﴾ its noun. ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of takun. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause lam takun is conjoined to an omitted clause. ﴿فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its khabar. ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ its khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَالسَّاعَةُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and al-sāʿa is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, which works like inna. ﴿رَيْبَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of lā; the clause is the khabar of al-sāʿa. ﴿قُلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿نَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّاعَةُ﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of nadrī. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ negative. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a shadda (إِنَّ); as a negative particle it is إِنْ.] ﴿نَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ظَنًّا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which works like laysa. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of mā; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَبَدا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَيِّئاتُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَحاقَ﴾ conjoined to badā. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what comes after them. ﴿يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kānū.

daas-irab:34-37.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿نَنْساكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause qīla is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿يَوْمِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هذا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of yawmikum. ﴿وَمَأْواكُمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿النَّارُ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَما﴾ a conjunction, and mā is negative. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿ناصِرِينَ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّكُمُ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and its noun. ﴿اتَّخَذْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿آياتِ﴾ its first object. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُزُواً﴾ its second object; the clause ittakhadhtum is the khabar of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of dhālikum, and the clause dhālikum is resumptive. ﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its object. ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُخْرَجُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلِلَّهِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ a badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿الْكِبْرِياءُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to al-samāwāt; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:1-7.t: ﴿حم﴾ its i'rab has already been given; ﴿تَنْزِيلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name is genitive by من, and both are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate); ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ two adjectives (ṣifa) of the Divine Name; ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis, and آيات is the postponed noun of inna; ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of آيات, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and the postponed mubtadaʾ is آيات in verse /5/ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the word آيات referred to is in verse 4.]», and both are conjoined to في السموات والأرض; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to خلقكم; ﴿يَبُثُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ دابَّةٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿آياتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of آيات; ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of قوم; ﴿وَاخْتِلافِ﴾ conjoined to خلقكم; ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَالنَّهارِ﴾ conjoined to الليل; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to اختلاف; ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ both attached to أنزل; ﴿مِنْ رِزْقٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from من السماء; ﴿فَأَحْيا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿مَوْتِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَتَصْرِيفِ﴾ conjoined to اختلاف; ﴿الرِّياحِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿آياتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of آيات; ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of قوم; ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿آياتُ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿نَتْلُوها﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿فَبِأَيِّ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and بأي are both attached to the verb after them; ﴿حَدِيثٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَآياتِهِ﴾ conjoined to الله; ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar; ﴿أَفَّاكٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ an adjective, and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:8-11.t: ﴿يَسْمَعُ آياتِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿يُصِرُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مُسْتَكْبِراً﴾ ḥāl; ﴿كَأَنْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, and its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَمْ يَسْمَعْها﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم, and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of kaʾan, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl; ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَ﴾ a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿عَلِمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿مِنْ آياتِنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿اتَّخَذَها﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿هُزُواً﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar; ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿مُهِينٌ﴾ an adjective of عذاب, and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك, and the clause أولئك is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and لا is negative; ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿كَسَبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; ﴿وَلا مَا اتَّخَذُوا﴾ conjoined to ما كسبوا; ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar; ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ an adjective, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿هذا هُدىً﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar; ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of الذين; ﴿مِنْ رِجْزٍ﴾ both attached to عذاب; ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي﴾ the Divine Name is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذي is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿سَخَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الْبَحْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لِتَجْرِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); ﴿الْفُلْكُ﴾ its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb سخر; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to تجري; ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ both attached to تجري; ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ conjoined to لتجري; ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and laʿalla and its noun; ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause لعلكم is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَسَخَّرَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both attached to an omitted verb forming the ṣila of the relative; ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to ما في السموات; ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ both attached to the omitted fronted khabar of inna; ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis, آيات is the postponed noun of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of آيات; ﴿يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of قوم; ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to يغفروا; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿يَغْفِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to a command (jawāb ṭalab), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause قل is resumptive; ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to يغفروا; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿أَيَّامَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause, and the fāʿil is latent, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb يغفروا; ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to يجزي; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of kāna, and the clause كانوا is the ṣila of ما.

daas-irab:15-20.t: ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عَمِلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿صالِحاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿فَلِنَفْسِهِ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the lām is a preposition, and a genitive noun, and both are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, and the implied verbal clause is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من; ﴿وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها﴾ conjoined to من عمل صالحا, and the i'rab is the same; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿إِلى رَبِّكُمْ﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and what is sworn by is omitted, and the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿آتَيْنا بَنِي﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ﴾ both conjoined to الكتاب; ﴿وَرَزَقْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَفَضَّلْناهُمْ﴾ conjoined to رزقناهم; ﴿عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَآتَيْناهُمْ بَيِّناتٍ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi, and بينات is its second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ both attached to بينات; ﴿فَمَا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿اخْتَلَفُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); ﴿جاءَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْعِلْمُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿بَغْياً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from ما and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿يَقْضِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna; ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿فِيما﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to what follows them, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; ﴿يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿جَعَلْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عَلى شَرِيعَةٍ﴾ both attached to the verb, and they stand in the place of the second object; ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ both attached to an adjective of شريعة; ﴿فَاتَّبِعْها﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive; ﴿تَتَّبِعْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿أَهْواءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila, and the clause لا تتبع is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَنْ﴾ a particle making the verb accusative; ﴿يُغْنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿عَنْكَ﴾ both attached to يغنوا; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to يغنوا as well; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إن is a particle resembling the verb; ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ its noun; ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿أَوْلِياءُ﴾ its khabar; ﴿بَعْضٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the khabar of inna; ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ; ﴿وَلِيُّ﴾ its khabar; ﴿الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿هذا بَصائِرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ both attached to the verb «[Translator's note: so in the source, although no verb is present; presumably attached to بصائر.]»; ﴿وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ conjoined; ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ both attached to رحمة; ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of قوم.

daas-irab:21-23.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئاتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi, and أن and what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar, stand in place of the two objects of حسب; ﴿كَالَّذِينَ﴾ the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of نجعلهم, and الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿سَواءً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مَحْياهُمْ﴾ the fāʿil of سواء; ﴿وَمَماتُهُمْ﴾ conjoined to محياهم; ﴿ساءَ﴾ an inflexible (jāmid) past verb expressing blame, whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿ما﴾ a complete (tāmma) indefinite noun, in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification); ﴿يَحْكُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of ما, and the clause ساء is resumptive; ﴿وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَلِتُجْزى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb, accusative by the implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to الحق; ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to تجزى; ﴿كَسَبَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl; ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مَنِ﴾ a relative, first mafʿūl bihi, and the second mafʿūl bihi is omitted; ﴿اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿هَواهُ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَأَضَلَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, fāʿil; ﴿عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾ ḥāl, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَخَتَمَ﴾ a past verb conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَلى سَمْعِهِ﴾ both attached to ختم; ﴿وَقَلْبِهِ﴾ conjoined to what preceded; ﴿وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً﴾ also conjoined to the ṣila clause; ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَهْدِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of من, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; as muḍāf ilayhi the word in the verse is اللَّهِ.]»; ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, the fāʾ is resumptive, and لا is negative; ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:24-26.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿حَياتُنَا﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿نَمُوتُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿وَنَحْيا﴾ conjoined to نموت, and the clause نموت is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative; ﴿يُهْلِكُنا﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; ﴿الدَّهْرُ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ما is negative; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿بِذلِكَ﴾ both attached to علم; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; ﴿يَظُنُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an adverbial conditional that does not make the verb jussive; ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿آياتُنا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ ḥāl; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿حُجَّتَهُمْ﴾ its fronted khabar; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle forming a maṣdar and making the verb accusative; ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) is in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of kāna; ﴿ائْتُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying; ﴿بِآبائِنا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿أَنْ﴾ a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive «[Translator's note: so written in the source; the verse has إِنْ.]»; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ما كان is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the non-jussive condition of إذا, with no grammatical position; ﴿قُلِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the clause قل is resumptive; ﴿ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, operating like inna; ﴿رَيْبَ﴾ its noun; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of lā, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and lākinna and its noun, and الناس is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:27-30.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an adverb of time; ﴿تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) for يوم; ﴿يَخْسَرُ﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation «[Translator's note: so in the source.]»; ﴿وَتَرى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿كُلَّ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿جاثِيَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mubtadaʾ «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; as mubtadaʾ the word in the verse is كُلُّ.]»; ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿تُدْعى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar; ﴿إِلى كِتابِهَا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause اليوم تجزون is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿هذا كِتابُنا﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿يَنْطِقُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿نَسْتَنْسِخُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of كنا, and the clause كنا is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause إنا is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila; ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and أما is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to أما, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil; ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is the khabar of الذين; ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ khabar; ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:22-26.t:
* I'rab:
(وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) You may make the speech conjoined to what preceded, so that it serves as a proof of the denial of equality between the two groups, or you may make it resumptive (istiʾnāf), introduced for this purpose. (وخلق الله السموات): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (والأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); and (بالحق) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or of the object. (وَلِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; (تجزى) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) أن after the causal lām. The speech is conjoined to His words (بالحق), because both the bāʾ and the lām can express cause, so the creation is given the recompense as its cause. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being "so that He may show by it His power, and so that every soul may be recompensed". Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose that it be the lām of consequence or outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba / al-ṣayrūra), i.e. and the matter came to be such that by them some people were guided and by them others went astray — and this is not far-fetched. The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا يظلمون) is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ) The hamza is of interrogation intended as a command, i.e. "inform me". (رأيت) is a verb and its agent; (من) is the first object of (رأيت), and the second is omitted, its implied form being "guided" (مهتديا). The clause (اتخذ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إلهه) is the first object of (اتخذ) and (هواه) its second object. (أضله الله): a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (على علم) is a ḥāl of the object, and this is preferable to making it a ḥāl of the agent, as al-Jalāl parsed it; the meaning is: Allah led him astray while he knew the truth, because the intensification in this is greater and the censure and condemnation of him more. (وَخَتَمَ عَلى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً) Conjoined to what preceded; the discussion of this verse has already been given in al-Baqara. (فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun in the sense of negation, i.e. no one guides him, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يهديه) is the khabar; and (من بعد الله) are attached to (يهديه). The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause, i.e. "do you persist in error?"; (لا) is negating, and (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped. (وَقالُوا: ما هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيا وَما يُهْلِكُنا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to refute their claims, since they used to claim that the perishing of souls depends on the passing of days and nights — more of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (ما) is negating; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (حياتنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (الدنيا) a khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; (الدنيا) is ordinarily parsed as an adjective of (حياتنا), which is the khabar of (هي)]. The clause (نموت) is resumptive, introduced to present more of their corrupt beliefs, and the clause (نحيا) is conjoined to it. The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (يهلكنا) is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الدهر) is the agent of (يهلكنا). (وَما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (بذلك) are attached to (علم); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (علم) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (إن) is negating, (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the clause (يظنون) is their khabar. (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ ما كانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا ائْتُوا بِآبائِنا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (تتلى) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and it is passive; (عليهم) are attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (بيّنات) is a ḥāl, i.e. clear in their indication. (ما) is negating; (كان) is a defective past verb; (حجتهم) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أن قالوا): أن and what it governs are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of (كان); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ائتوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (بآبائنا) are attached to (ائتوا); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring them"; (صادقين) is the khabar of (كنتم). (قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) (قل) is an imperative verb; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحييكم) its khabar; (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay, pointing to the interval separating life and death; (يميتكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and an object; (ثم) is a conjunction as before; (يجمعكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and the kāf is the object; (إلى يوم القيامة) are attached to (يجمعكم). (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ريب) is its noun and (فيه) its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl of (يوم القيامة). (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar.

* Benefits:
Al-dahr (time) in the language is the duration of the world's existence, from "dahrahum amrun", i.e. time struck them with it. In al-Qāmūs: «dahrahum amrun, on the pattern of manaʿa: something hateful befell them; and they are madhūrun bihim and madhūrūn». It was the custom of the Arabs, when misfortune struck them, to ascribe it to time (al-dahr), believing that it is what does whatever it wills; and you see their poetry speaking out in complaint against time, so that this is found even in the poetry of Muslims. Ibn Durayd said in his Maqṣūra:
يا دهر إن لم تك عتبى فاتئد ... في إروادك والعتبى سوا
(O Time, if there is to be no making amends, then go gently in your pace — and making amends is the same.)
Abū al-ʿAlāʾ refuted the views of the Dahriyya (materialists) in his Luzūmiyyāt, saying:
ودان أناس بالجزاء وكونه ... وقال رجال إنما أنتم بقل
(Some people believed in recompense and its coming to pass, while other men said: you are nothing but herbage.)
This is a reply to the Dahriyya, who say that the world is eternal by nature, has always been so, and did not come into being through the act of an originator, and that people are like plants: they sprout and return through death to dry stubble. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said, refuting Ibn al-Rāwandī and his book al-Tāj, in Risālat al-Ghufrān, among what he said: «As for Ibn al-Rāwandī, he was not guided to what is right; and as for his Crown (Tāj), it is not fit to be even a sandal. Is his Crown anything but as the soothsayer woman said: "Uff and tuff, a sock and a slipper"?» And the Prophet ﷺ said: «Do not revile time, for Allah is time», i.e. because He, the Exalted, is the One who does whatever He wills, not time. The ḥadīth was narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others from Abū Hurayra.

dervis-irab:27-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جاثِيَةً) One says: jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi juthuwwan (he knelt on his knees); I saw him kneeling (jāthiyan) before him, and I saw them kneeling (juthiyyan) at his side. In the ḥadīth: «I shall be the first to kneel for the dispute before Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection». They knelt facing one another on their knees (tajāthaw), and he knelt facing his opponent (ajāthā khaṣmahu mujāthātan); and so-and-so became a juthwa (heap) of earth. Ṭarafa said:
ترى جثوتين من تراب عليهما ... صفائح صمّ من صفيح منضّد
(You see two heaps of earth upon which lie hard slabs, from stacked slabs.)
That is: I see the grave of the miser and of the generous man as two mounds of earth with broad hard stones upon them, among graves upon which broad stones have been stacked. The wording of al-Qurṭubī: «There are five interpretations of al-jāthiya. The first: Mujāhid said: crouching ready (mustawfiza); Sufyān said: the one crouching ready is the one of whom nothing touches the ground but his knees and the tips of his fingers; al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: and that is at the Reckoning. The second: gathered together, said by Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is, you see the people of every religion gathered together. The third: set apart, said by ʿIkrima. The fourth: humbled, in the dialect of Quraysh. The fifth: kneeling on the knees, said by al-Ḥasan. Al-juthuww is sitting on the knees; one says jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi yajthū and yajthī, juthuwwan and juthiyyan, on the pattern fuʿūl in both; this has already been discussed in Maryam. The origin of al-juthwa is a group of anything. Then it was said that it is specific to the disbelievers, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām; and it was said that it is general for the believer and the disbeliever, awaiting the Reckoning. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the Prophet ﷺ said: It is as though I see you kneeling on your knees short of Hell.» Further, it has been read jādhiya, with dhāl; and al-judhuww is more of a crouching-ready posture than al-juthuww, because the jādhī is the one who sits on the tips of his toes.
(نَسْتَنْسِخُ) That is, We have the angels write down your deeds. In al-Asās:
«I copied (nasakhtu) my book from so-and-so's book, intasakhtuhu and istansakhtuhu, with the same meaning; and istinsākh can mean having something written (istiktāb): "Indeed We were having written down (nastansikhu)". This is an old copy (nuskha) and old copies (nusakh).» The meaning is: We command the angels to copy what you used to do and to record it; so what is meant by naskh here is not cancelling one thing and putting another in its place.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) Resumptive speech, introduced to generalise the power after specifying it with giving life, causing death and gathering, because the meaning of owner is one who disposes of what he owns as he wills. (لله) is a fronted khabar (predicate), and (ملك السموات والأرض) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb attached to (يخسر); the clause (تقوم الساعة) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, and it is a badal (substitute) of (يوم تقوم); the tanwīn in (يومئذ) is a tanwīn of compensation for a clause, i.e. "the day the Hour is established". It was also said that what governs (ويوم تقوم) is what (الملك) indicates; they said: because the heaven and the earth will be changed, so it is as though it were said "and to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and the dominion on the Day of Resurrection"; on this view (يومئذ) is accusative by (يخسر). (يخسر المبطلون): a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً، كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى إِلى كِتابِهَا) The wāw is a conjunction; (ترى) is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) agent, its implied form being "you"; (كل أمة) is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if the seeing is cognitive, but the context of the speech favours its being visual; (جاثية) is a second object on the first view and a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the second. (كل أمة) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (تدعى إلى كتابها) is the khabar. (الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (تجزون); (تجزون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) is the second object of (تجزون); and the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. it will be said to them: "Today you are recompensed". (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تعملون) is its khabar; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (هذا كِتابُنا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ) (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (كتابنا) a khabar, and the clause (ينطق) a second khabar or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. It is also permissible for (كتابنا) to be a badal of (هذا), with the clause (ينطق) as the khabar of (هذا). (بالحق) is a ḥāl, and (عليكم) are attached to (ينطق). The meaning of the book's speaking will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (إن) and its noun; the clause (كنّا) is the khabar of (إنّا); the clause (نستنسخ) is the khabar of (كنّا); (ما) is a direct object; the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (ما); and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and of detailing the summary understood from His words (ينطق عليكم بالحق) or from (تجزون); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). (فيدخلهم): the fāʾ links the apodosis of (أما), and the clause (يدخلهم ربهم في رحمته) is the khabar of (الذين). (ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ) Its i'rab has been given many times. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; and the apodosis of (أما) is omitted, its implied form being "then it will be said to them". The hamza is of interrogation, and the fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted apodosis; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (تكن) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); the meaning is "did not My messengers come to you, and were not…". (آياتي) is the noun of (تكن), and the clause (تتلى عليكم) is its khabar. (فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (استكبرتم) is a verb and its agent; (كنتم): (كان) and its noun; (قوما) is its khabar, and (مجرمين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق» there is an implicit metaphor: the book is likened to a witness who delivers his testimony truthfully; the thing to which it is likened is omitted, and one of its concomitants — speaking the testimony — is borrowed for it.
2- In His words «فيدخلهم في رحمته» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is that of the occupant (al-ḥāliyya), i.e. into His Garden; because a person does not dwell in mercy, since it is an abstract notion; he dwells only in its place. So using "mercy" for its place is a trope in which the occupant is mentioned and the place is meant, and its relation is that of the occupant.

dervis-irab:32-37.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ لا رَيْبَ فِيها قُلْتُمْ ما نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what preceded because it is part of what is said to them. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; (قيل) is a passive past verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (إن) with its noun and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (الساعة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا ريب فيها) is its khabar. It was also said that (الساعة) is conjoined to the position of (إن) and its noun together, because إن and its noun have a position, namely nominative by being the subject. (والساعة) was also read in the accusative, conjoined to (الوعد). The clause [ما الساعة] is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (ندري), because the verb is suspended (ʿulliqat) by the interrogative. The clause (قلتم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ما) is negating; (ندري) is a nominative imperfect verb; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (الساعة) is its khabar. (إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ) (إن) is negating; (نظن) is a nominative imperfect verb; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (ظنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). This construction is one of the difficulties around which the grammarians and exegetes have hummed at length; we shall give you more on it in the section on Benefits. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating mā; (نحن) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (مستيقنين) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما). (وَبَدا لَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) The wāw is resumptive; (بدا) is a past verb; (لهم) are attached to (بدا); (سيئات) is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (حاق بهم) is conjoined to (بدا لهم); (ما) is the agent of (حاق); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (به) are attached to (يستهزئون); and the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنْساكُمْ كَما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قيل) is a passive past verb; (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (ننساكم); (كما) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نسيتم) is a verb and its agent; (لقاء يومكم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The adverb has been used broadly, so that what occurs in it is annexed to it, in the manner of His words "the plotting of the night" (makr al-layl). (هذا) is a naʿt of (يومكم) or a badal (substitute) of it. (وَمَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (مأواكم) is a fronted khabar and (النار) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the reverse is permissible. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (ناصرين) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ذلِكُمْ بِأَنَّكُمُ اتَّخَذْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ هُزُواً) (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the great punishment prepared for them. (بأنكم): أن and what is in its domain are in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of (ذلك). (أن) and its noun, and the clause (اتخذتم) is its khabar; (آيات الله) is the first object of (اتخذتم), and (هزوا) is the second object of (اتخذتم). (وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) The wāw is a conjunction; (غرّتكم) is a past verb and a fronted direct object; (الحياة) is a postponed agent, and (الدنيا) is a naʿt of (الحياة). (فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْها وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (يخرجون); (لا) is negating; (يخرجون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; (منها) are attached to (يخرجون). (ولا) is conjoined to what preceded; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يستعتبون) is the khabar. (فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (لله) is a fronted khabar and (الحمد) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (رب السموات) is a badal or naʿt of (لله), and likewise what follows it. (وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (له) is a fronted khabar and (الكبرياء) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الكبرياء), and it may be attached to the [notion of] being established to which the first adverbial phrase is attached; some chose that it be attached to (الكبرياء) itself, because it is a maṣdar. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and (العزيز الحكيم) are two khabars of it.

* Rhetoric:
1- The synecdochic trope (al-majāz al-mursal) or the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «وقيل اليوم ننساكم» etc. there is a majāz mursal whose relation is causality, because forgetting is the cause of leaving; when a thing is forgotten it is left and entirely neglected. Some said: it is also permissible to regard the pronoun of address as containing a metaphor by allusion (istiʿāra bi-l-kināya), likening them to a forgotten thing in their being left in the punishment and no heed being paid to them, with the attribution of forgetting being the indicator (qarīna) of the metaphor.
2- The shift of person (al-iltifāt): this is in His words «فاليوم لا يخرجون منها»; He shifted from address to the third person when He reached this state to which they had come, for they deserve to be dropped from the rank of being addressed, out of contempt and disdain for them.

* Benefits:
We pointed to the difficulty arising in His words, Exalted is He, «إن نظن إلا ظنا», because the emphatic maṣdar may not occur as an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); one does not say "I did not strike except a striking", since it has no benefit, being equivalent to saying "I did not strike except I struck". It is established among the grammarians that the governing word may be emptied for whatever follows it of all the governed elements except the absolute object; so one does not say "I did not think except a thinking", because the locus of negation and affirmation — namely thinking — is one and the same, whereas restriction is conceivable only when their loci differ. The following is what the grammarians said:
Al-Mubarrad said: its origin is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking" (in naḥnu illā naẓunnu ẓannan). He means that the locus of negation is omitted, namely the speaker's being engaged in some act or other; that is the locus of negation, and the locus of affirmation is his thinking a thinking. So the word (إلا), though placed later in the wording, is placed earlier in the implied structure. The import of the restriction is the affirmation of conjecture for themselves and the negation of everything other than it; among everything other than it is certainty, and it is what is intended to be negated; but He negated everything other than conjecture absolutely, for emphasis in negating certainty, and for that reason it was reinforced by His words (وما نحن بمستيقنين).
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he interpreted it as the omission of an adjective of the maṣdar, so that it becomes specifying rather than emphatic, its implied form being "except a weak conjecture"; or as (نظن) being made to carry the meaning of "we believe" (naʿtaqidu), so that (ظنا) is a direct object.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words (إن نظن إلا ظنا)? I say: its origin is "we think a thinking", and its meaning is the affirmation of conjecture together with the negation of everything else; and the negation of everything other than conjecture was further emphasised by His words: (وما نحن بمستيقنين).»
Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī as is his habit, saying: «This is the speech of one who has no awareness of the grammatical rule that emptying [for the exception] occurs with all the governed elements — agent, object and others — except the emphatic maṣdar, for it does not occur with it.»
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he said: «Its implied form is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking", so (إلا) has been postponed; were it not for this implied form, the meaning would be "we do not think except a thinking". It was also said that it is in its proper place, because (نظن) may have the meaning of knowledge and of doubt, so doubt was excepted, i.e. we have no belief except doubt.»

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٍ آيَاتٌ﴾.
He says: in the creation of human beings and of all besides them that have souls there are signs. الآيات is read with the genitive [ending -āti] in the interpretation of the accusative, referred back to His saying: ﴿إنّ فى السمَّواتِ والأرْضِ لآياتٍ﴾; and what strengthens the genitive in it is that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: ﴿لآيات﴾, and in the reading of Ubayy: لآيات لآيات لآياتٍ, all three of them. The nominative is the reading of the people, by resumption (istiʾnāf) in what comes after إنّ. The Arabs say: "I have money owed by you (إن لى عليك مالا), and by your brother much money", putting the second in the accusative and in the nominative.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وفى اختلاف اللّيل والنهارِ"; this strengthens the genitive of الاختلاف. Had someone put it in the nominative and said: "and the alternation of the night and the day are also signs", making the alternation the signs, [it would be possible], but we have not heard it from any of the readers. He said: and had someone put الآيات in the nominative while it has the lām, it would have been correct. He said: al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
إنّ الخلافة بعدهم لذميمة * وخلائف طرف لمما أحقر
(The caliphate after them is surely blameworthy, and [its] upstart successors are of the most contemptible.)
He brought in the lām, while it is only a response to إنّ, and he used the nominative because the speech is built on the interpretation of إنّ.
«[Translator's note: the second hemistich is obscure as transmitted; the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ﴾.
Its meaning in origin is a reported speech in the position of a command, as in your saying: "Say to those who believe: forgive." When the command appears explicitly it is jussive, because it is a command; and when it is in the form of a statement, as in His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِلذين آمَنوا يَغْفِروا﴾, ﴿وقُلْ لِّعبادى يَقُولُوا﴾ and ﴿قُلْ لِعبادِىَ الذين آمَنُوا يُقيمُوا الصلاةَ﴾, it is jussive by resemblance to the requital (jazāʾ) and the condition (sharṭ), as though it were your saying: "Stand, and you will meet good"; but it is not so. Rather, the Arabs, when speech comes out in the pattern of something else that is close to it, inflect it with that one's inflection; and this is of that kind, and we have mentioned it in more than one place. His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذينَ آمَنُو يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ أيّامَ اللّهِ﴾ was revealed concerning the polytheists, before the Prophet, Allah bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to fight the people of Mecca.
His saying: ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْماً بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it: لنجزى, with nūn, and the people after him read ﴿لِيجْزِىَ قوما﴾, with yāʾ; and they are the same, in the position of His saying: ﴿وقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ and "وقد خلقناك من قبل". Some reader, as was reported to me, read: ليُجزَى قَوْماً, and on its face that is an error (laḥn); but if he implied in "يجزى" a verbal noun that takes the nominative, as you say: "He was given a garment", "so that that requital may be given to a people", then it is a valid view.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةٍ﴾.
On a religion, a creed and a way; all of that is said.
«[Translator's note: the source has «يقل», evidently «يقال» ("is said").]»

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾.
You put الله in the nominative, and that is the [proper] way of i'rab when a noun comes after إنَّ and its khabar (predicate): put it in the nominative, whether a verb is with it or not.
As for the one with no verb with it, it is His saying: ﴿أنّ اللّهَ برىٌ من المشركينَ ورسولُه﴾; and as for the one with a verb with it, it is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿واللّهُ وَلىُّ المتقين﴾.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾.
Al-ijtirāḥ is committing (iqtirāf) and earning.
His saying: ﴿سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾: you put سواء in the accusative and in the nominative, while المحيا and الممات are in the position of the nominative, in the same way as the saying: "I saw the people, equal (سواءً) their young and their old" [174/b]. You put سواء in the accusative because you make it a verb (fiʿl) for what returns to the people of mention of them, and what returns to the people and all nouns by mention of them, its verb having preceded; so make the verb inflected by the first noun. You say: "I passed by a people equal their young and their old", and "I saw a people equal their young and their old".
And likewise the nominative. The Arabs sometimes take (سواءً) in the manner of a noun, in the position of حسبك (sufficient for you), so they say: "I saw a people, equal are their young and their old", so it is like your saying: "I passed by a man, sufficient for you is his brother". Had you put مستوٍ (equal, a participle) in place of سواء, you would not use the nominative, but would make it follow what precedes it, unlike سواء, because مستو is a description of the people, while سواء is like the maṣdar, and the maṣdar is a noun.
And had you put المحيا and الممات in the accusative, it would be a valid view, meaning that you make them equal in their life and their death.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it (غَشْوَة), with fatḥa on the ghayn and without adding an alif to it, and the people read it (غِشاوَة). It is as though غشاوة were a noun, and غشوة something that covered it in a single occurrence, like al-rajfa, al-raḥma and al-marra.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا﴾.
Someone may say: how did He say "we die and we live" when they deny the resurrection? He meant only: we die, and our sons come after us; so He made the act of their sons like their own act; and this is frequent in Arabic.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَآ إِلاَّ ٱلدَّهْرُ﴾.
They say: nothing but the length of time and the passing of days, nights, months and years.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وما يُهْلِكُنا إِلاّ دَهْرٌ", as though: nothing but time passing.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً﴾.
He means: the people of every religion kneeling, he says: gathered for the reckoning. Then He said: ﴿كُلُّ أمَّةٍ تُدْعَىٰ إِلَىٰ كِتَابِهَا﴾: he says: to its reckoning; and it is from the saying of Allah: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِه﴾ and ﴿بشماله﴾.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
Al-istinsākh is that the two angels raise up a man's deeds, small and great, and Allah confirms of his deeds what carries reward or punishment, and discards from them the idle talk in which there is neither reward nor punishment, such as your saying "come here", "come" and "go". That is al-istinsākh.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَفَلَمْ﴾.
He implied the verb of saying: "then it is said: أفلم". Like it: ﴿فأما الَّذين اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ أكَفَرْتُمْ﴾; its meaning is: "then it is said: أكفرتم", and Allah knows best. That is because أمّا must be answered with fāʾ, but it dropped when the verb that was implied dropped.

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ إِنَّ وعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهَا﴾: you put الساعة in the nominative, and that is the [usual] way of speech; and if you put it in the accusative, it is correct; Ḥamza al-Zayyāt read it so. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وَإذَا قِيلَ إنَّ وَعْدَ اللّهِ حقُّ وإن السَّاعةَ لا رَيْبَ فيها". So you have learned the two views, and they have been explained in other places.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقِيلَ ٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَاكُمْ﴾.
We leave you in the Fire just as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours; he says: just as you abandoned working for the meeting of this Day of yours.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ لاَ يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا وَلاَ هُمْ يُسْتَعَتَبُونَ﴾.
He says: they are not given a return of speech after they enter the Fire.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «والذين كفروا......» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «هذا هدى»; the clause «لهم عذاب» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; the preposition «من رجز» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «الله الذي»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The preposition «بأمره» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الفلك»; the preposition «فيه» is attached to «تجري»; the maṣdar (verbal noun) «ولتبتغوا» is genitive (majrūr), conjoined to the first genitive maṣdar «لتجري»; and the clause «ولعلكم تشكرون» is conjoined to the single-word genitive maṣdar «ولتبتغوا».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما»; the preposition «منه» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «جميعا»; and the clause «يتفكرون» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "forgive", meaning: if you tell them, they will forgive — those meant being the believers, who comply whenever he commands them. The clause «يغفروا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليجزي» is genitive (majrūr) and attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قل», and the preposition «بما» is attached to «يجزي».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «مَنْ»: conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject); «صالحًا»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). His words «فلنفسه»: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then his deed is for himself"; the implied form of the second apodosis (jawāb) is "then his evil-doing is against himself". The clause «ترجعون» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «مَنْ عَمِل».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition «على العالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فضَّلْناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «بينات»: second object; the preposition «من الأمر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بينات». The clause «فما اختلفوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «آتيناهم»; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition «من بعد» is attached to «اختلفوا»; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «بغيا»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); «بينهم» is an adverb attached to a naʿt of «بغيا». The two adverbs «بينهم» and «يوم» are attached to «يقضي», as is «فيما»; and the preposition «فيه» is attached to «يختلفون».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «ثم» is a particle of resumption, and the clause after it is resumptive. The preposition «على شريعة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل», and the clause «فاتبعها» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «جعلناك».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيئا»; «شيئا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a little or a great sufficing". The clause «وإن الظالمين ... » is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «إنهم لن يغنوا», and the clause «بعضهم أولياء» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The preposition «للناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بصائر»; the preposition «لقوم» is attached to a naʿt of «رحمة».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن نجعلهم» stands in place of the two objects of «حَسِبَ»; the preposition «كالذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «نجعل». «سواء» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the preposition «كالذين», i.e. "they being equal"; «محياهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «سواء». The clause «ساء ما يحكمون» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil of «ساء», and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "their judgement".

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «وخلق» is resumptive; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلق». His words «ولتجزى»: the wāw is conjunctive, and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to something implied, i.e. "so that it may point to His power and so that … may be recompensed". The clause «وهم لا يظلمون» is a ḥāl.
