(Had Qufayra given birth to a dog's whelp, the dogs would have been reviled through that whelp.)
there is no proof in it. I saw Abū Isḥāq hold that its implied form is: "had Qufayra given birth to the dogs", with «جرو كلب» accusative as a vocative.

nahhas-irab:16-18.t:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ وَرَزَقْناهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ وَفَضَّلْناهُمْ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ) (16) (وَآتَيْناهُمْ بَيِّناتٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا إِلاَّ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ) (17) (ثُمَّ جَعَلْناكَ عَلى شَرِيعَةٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ فَاتَّبِعْها وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) (18)
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ): Mālik ibn Dīnār said: I asked Mujāhid about الحكم and he said: understanding (al-lubb). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: الشريعة is the clear way and the straight course; from it is شريعة النهر (the watering-place of the river), and طريق شارع, that is, a clear, plain road. شرائع الدين are what Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has laid down for His servants so that they may know them. The plural of شريعة is شرائع; it is reported that one also says شِرَع, and in reality شرع is the plural of شِرعة.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: (بَعْضُهُمْ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أولياء» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنّ». It is permissible to put بعضهم in the accusative as a badal (substitute) of «الظالمين». (وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ): a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the accusative is permissible by conjoining it to [the noun of] «إنّ». Al-Kisāʾī said: He said (هذا بَصائِرُ) and did not say «هذه بصائر» because He meant the Quran and the admonition.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
(الَّذِينَ) is in the position of the nominative by «حسب». (أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): «أن» and its ṣila stand for the two objects [of حسب]; the hāʾ and mīm are in the position of the accusative as the first object of «نجعلهم», and (كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) is in the position of the second object. (سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) [i.e. «سواءٌ»]. This is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read (سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ) with سواء in the accusative. Abū ʿUbayd said: and thus he reads it in the accusative, by «نجعلهم» falling upon it. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: some grammarians permitted (سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ) [i.e. with محياهم ومماتهم also in the accusative], and it has been read so. [Translator's note: the source prints the three readings with the same vowelling; the case endings intended are given in brackets as the discussion implies.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading, (سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ) [i.e. «سواءٌ»], is the one on which the authority of the Companions, the Successors and the grammarians has agreed, as was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, from Musaddad, from Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Qays, from Mujāhid, on His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: (سَواءً مَحْياهُمْ وَمَماتُهُمْ): he said: The believer dies upon his faith and is resurrected upon it, and the disbeliever dies upon his disbelief and is resurrected upon it. And from Abū al-Dardāʾ: he said: People will be resurrected upon what they died upon; and similar to this from Tamīm and Ḥudhayfa. So the authority has agreed that it is not permissible to read except with the nominative, and that whoever reads the accusative has departed from these interpretations. On this [view], (سَواءً) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and there is no ground for its accusative, because the meaning is that the believers are alike in their life and their death, and the disbelievers are alike in their life and their death.
Then, returning to the accusative, it would be from another angle, namely an angle that al-Akhfash Saʿīd mentioned; he said: the meaning would be "or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make their life and their death alike, like the life and death of the believers?" On this approach the accusative is permissible; yet even on this approach the preferred choice according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, is also the nominative, and the examples of all the grammarians are with the nominative. You say: ظننت زيدا سواءٌ أبوه وأمّه ("I thought Zayd [to be such that] his father and mother are alike"); they permit the accusative, but their examples are with the nominative. The most astonishing thing in this is: if the examples of the grammarians are thus, how did al-Kisāʾī read it and Abū ʿUbayd choose it?
As for the reading with the accusative, «سواءً محياهم ومماتهم», there are two ways in it. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "in their life and in their death", then «في» was dropped; he holds that it is accusative as [an adverb of] time. The other way is that «محياهم ومماتهم» be a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ and mīm in «نجعلهم», in the sense: "or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make their life and their death alike, like those who believe and do righteous deeds", that is, like the life and death of those who believe and do righteous deeds. (ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ): if you make «ما» definite, its position is nominative; if you make it indefinite, its position is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz — specification).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: The lām of purpose (lām kay) must be attached to a verb, either implied or overt; here it is implied, that is: "and so that every soul may be requited for what it has earned, He did that".

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
(مَنِ) is in the position of the accusative. The scholars have three views on its meaning. The most important of them is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on (أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ): he said: the disbeliever adopted his religion without guidance from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and without proof. Al-Ḥasan said: he is the one who, whenever he desires something, does not refrain from it. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: one of them would worship a thing, then when he saw something else better than it, he would worship it and abandon the other. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of al-Ḥasan is by way of comparison, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبارَهُمْ وَرُهْبانَهُمْ أَرْباباً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ [al-Tawba: 31]; but more consistent with the sequence of the verse is that it be about the disbelievers.
(وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ): there are three views on it. Among them: the meaning is that He led him astray from the reward, with knowledge on His part that he does not deserve it. The second view: the meaning is "with knowledge on his part that his worship does not benefit him". These two views were not held by any of the early [scholars]. The most fitting thing said about the verse is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on (وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ): he said: in His prior knowledge. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: (وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ), that is, upon knowledge He had of him. (وَخَتَمَ عَلى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ): Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it in Sūrat «al-Baqara».
(وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً): in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], (وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً) is narrated with fatḥa on the ghayn [i.e. «غَشاوة»], which is the dialect of Rabīʿa, according to what al-Farrāʾ supposes. The reading of ʿIkrima is «غُشاوة» with ḍamma on the ghayn, which is the dialect of ʿUkl. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the alif may be dropped from it, and when the alif is dropped there are three dialectal forms in it: غَشْوة, غُشْوة and غِشْوة [Translator's note: the three are printed alike in the source]. As for the meaning, it is close: it is only a figure, that is, he does not see the truth, so he is like one over whose sight is a covering. Except that the more common [pattern] in the speech of the Arabs for the like of this is فِعالة, and that is in everything that envelops a thing, such as عمامة (turban), and likewise ولاية.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
(وَقالُوا ما هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيا): we have mentioned it, except that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the meaning is "there is nothing but our worldly life; we die and live [again], according to your claim"; and he considered it far-fetched that the meaning be "we live and die" by way of putting first and putting later, saying: this is permissible only where the meaning is known, as in وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي [Āl ʿImrān: 43]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The scholars of Arabic disagree with him on this, and permit putting first and putting later with the wāw in every place.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning of (وَما يُهْلِكُنا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ) is: the length of time and the passing of days, nights, months and years. A group spoke about the meaning of the verse. Some of them said: these are a people who did not know Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; had they known Him, they would have known that it is He who destroys them and causes them to die. Some said: it may be that they knew Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, but held that these afflictions that befall them are only due to causes and the turning of the celestial sphere; they say this without proof or knowledge. And some said: these are a group of Arabs who knew Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, as indicated by their saying ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفى [al-Zumar: 3], and among them were some who believed in the resurrection. Zuhayr said [metre: al-ṭawīl], verse 419:
يؤخّر فيوضع في كتاب فيدّخر ... ليوم الحساب أو يعجّل فينقم
(It is deferred, placed in a record and stored up for the Day of Reckoning, or hastened and avenged.)
However, they were ignorant people who did not know that afflictions are decreed by Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. This is the soundest thing narrated about the verse and the most consistent with its sequence; the proof has been established for it by the apparent sense, and because it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said, on His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: وَما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ: he said: they said "we will not be resurrected" without knowledge, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: وَما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ.

nahhas-irab:25-26.t:
(ما كانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ): [حجتهم is] the khabar (predicate) of kāna; (إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا) is its noun (ism). «ما كان حجّتُهم» in the nominative is permissible, as the noun of kāna, because الحجّة and الاحتجاج are one, the khabar then being (إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا), that is, "except their saying".
(قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ): the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. (ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ) is conjoined to it, and likewise (ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ). (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): it was said: that is, they are like one who does not know; and it was said: it is incumbent upon them to know.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): that is, so He is able to bring you to life. (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ): an adverb (ẓarf), accusative by «يخسر».

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
(وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً): (كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ) [the second, in كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى] is [nominative] as a mubtadaʾ (subject); al-Kisāʾī permitted «كلَّ أمة» [in the accusative] as a repetition of the first كلّ. We have mentioned the meaning of (تُدْعى إِلى كِتابِهَا), and that the most fitting thing said about it is that [it is called] to what has been written against it of good and evil, as is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: from Thursday to Thursday, what the angels, peace be upon them, have written against the children of Ādam is presented, and from it is copied what is to be requited of good and evil, and the rest is discarded. So the meaning on this [view] is: every community is called to what has been written against it and recorded, and it is bound by it, whether obedience or disobedience; and if it was disbelief, it is made to stand by it and made to follow what it used to worship.
As was read before Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn Abī Isrāʾīl, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He, on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: «Do you harm one another [in crowding] over [seeing] the moon on the night of the full moon, when there is no cloud before it?» They said: "No." He said: «Then do you harm one another over [seeing the sun at] midday, when there is no cloud before it?» They said: "No." He said: «By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, you will see Him as you see it.» He said: «The servant will meet his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say: "O So-and-so (ay ful), did I not honour you, make you a chief, marry you, subject horses and camels to you, and leave you to lead and take the fourth [of the spoils]?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord." He will say: "Did you think that you would meet Me?" He will say: "No, my Lord." He will say: "Then I forget you as you forgot Me." Then He will say to the second the like of that, and he will say to Him the like of that, and He will reply to him the like of that. Then He will say to the third the like of that, and he will say: "My Lord, I believed in You and in Your Book, and I fasted, prayed and gave charity." He said: Then He will say: "Shall We not send Our witness against you?" He said: He will think to himself: "Who is this who will bear witness against me?" Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, will seal his mouth and say to his thigh: "Speak!" And his thigh, his bones and his flesh will speak of what he used to do. That is so that he has no excuse left for himself; that is the one with whom He is angry, and that is the hypocrite.» He said: «Then a caller will call: "Let every community follow what it used to worship." And the devils and the crosses will be followed by their devotees, and we will remain, O believers.» He said: «Then our Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He, will come to us and say: "Who are these?" They will say: "Your believing servants; we believed in You and did not associate anything with You, and this is our station until our Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He, comes to us and rewards us."» He said: «Then they will set off until they come to the bridge, and on it are hooks of fire snatching people. There intercession becomes permitted: "O Allah, grant safety!" When they have crossed the bridge, everyone who spent a pair of whatever wealth he owned in the way of Allah — all the keepers of Paradise will call him: "O servant of Allah, O Muslim, this is good, so come!"» Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is nothing against this servant [Translator's note: so in the source, «لا ترى عليه»; the sense is "there is no harm for him"] in leaving one gate and entering by another." He said: Then he struck his shoulder and said: «By the One in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be one of them.»
And it was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, [from] ʿĪsā ibn Ḥammād [Translator's note: the source has «أحمد بن شعيب بن عيسى بن حماد», apparently with «عن» dropped], who said: al-Layth ibn Saʿd informed us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Abū Hurayra, who said: «The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He, on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you harm one another over [seeing] the sun when there is no cloud before it? And do you harm one another over [seeing] the moon on the night of the full moon?" They said: "No." He said: "Thus will you see Him."» He said: «Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection and say: "Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it." So whoever used to worship the sun will follow the sun, whoever used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and whoever used to worship the false deities (al-ṭawāghīt) will follow the false deities; and this community will remain, with its hypocrites. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, will come to them in the form that they know and say: "I am your Lord." They will say: "You are our Lord," and they will follow Him. The path (al-ṣirāṭ) will be laid across the midst of Jahannam, and I and my community will be the first to cross it. None will speak except the messengers, peace be upon them, and the supplication of the messengers on that day is: "O Allah, grant safety, grant safety!" In Jahannam there are hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān — have you seen the saʿdān? — for they are like the thorns of the saʿdān, except that none knows the extent of their size but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. They will snatch people according to their deeds. Then when Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, wills to bring out of the Fire by His mercy whomever He wills, He will command the angels to bring out whoever did not associate anything with Allah, of those who say "There is no god but Allah", among those He wills to have mercy upon. They will recognise them in the Fire by the traces of prostration; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has forbidden the Fire to consume the traces of prostration on the son of Ādam. So they will bring them out of the Fire, having been charred, and the water of life will be poured over them, and they will grow as a seed grows in the silt carried by a flood.»
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the explanation of «تضارّون», we dictate it from what we took from Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], with an explanation of all that is in it, such as needs no addition. He said: What came in the ḥadīth is with the light [consonant], «تُضارون» and «تُضامون», and it has a good justification in Arabic. This is a place whose explanation needs to be pursued thoroughly, for it is a foundation of [the creed of] the Sunna and the Community. Its meaning is: no harm (ḍayr) and no injury (ḍaym) will befall you in seeing Him, that is, you will see Him so that you are all equal in the seeing, and none of you will harm another. He said: The lexicographers held two other views. They said: «لا تُضارّون» with the rāʾ doubled and «لا تُضامّون» with the mīm doubled, with ḍamma on the tāʾ. He said: and some of them said it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and with the rāʾ and mīm doubled [«تَضارّون», «تَضامّون»], in the sense of «تتضارّون» and «تتضامّون». The explanation of this is that none of you will harm another, that is, none of you will differ from another in that. One says ضاررت الرجل أضارّه مضارّة وضرارا when you differ with him. And the meaning of «لا تضامّون في رؤيته» is: you will not press against one another, one saying to the other "Show it to me", as they do when looking at the new moon.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً مِّنْهُ﴾.
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: From Him is the light, from Him is the sun, and from Him is the moon.
And it is read ﴿جَمِيعاً مِنَّةً﴾, in the sense of: He bestowed it as a favour (minna) [Translator's note: i.e. accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun)].
And it is read ﴿مِنَّةٌ﴾, in the sense of: that is a favour [Translator's note: i.e. khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject)].
And ﴿مَنُّةُ﴾ is permissible, on the basis that it is a maṣdar, as the Exalted said: ﴿صُنْعَ
اللهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, they do not care about the favours of Allah, i.e. they do not know that He bestowed them upon them, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَذَكِّرْهُمْ بِأَيَّامِ اللهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that the meaning is: they do not hope for the Resurrection, i.e. they do not believe in it.
And Qatāda said: This verse is abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا
المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلأَمْرِ فَٱتَّبِعْهَا وَلاَ تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: The sharīʿa is the obligations, the prescribed limits, the command and the prohibition.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Sharīʿa in the language is the way (al-madhhab) and the creed (al-milla). From it comes "so-and-so embarked (sharaʿa) upon such-and-such", and from it [comes al-shāriʿ (the main road), because it is a way to the destination; so the sharīʿa is what Allah has laid down for His servants of the religion, and the plural is al-sharāʾiʿ], meaning the ways.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا بَصَائِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.
That is, this Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾.
﴿ٱجْتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ means: they earned evil deeds. From it is ﴿ويَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُمْ بِالنَّهَارِ﴾, and from it is al-jawāriḥ, i.e. the earners [i.e. hunting animals; also the limbs].
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The believer dies a believer and is resurrected a believer, and the disbeliever dies a disbeliever and is resurrected a disbeliever.
And it is read: ﴿سَوَاءٌ مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾.
And al-Aʿmash read: ﴿سَوَاءٍ مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first reading is better in terms of meaning according to Mujāhid's view, and it is also finer in the view of the grammarians in terms of i'rab (grammatical analysis).
And al-Aʿmash's reading is on the basis of badal (substitute), and according to al-Farrāʾ it has the sense of a ẓarf (adverb).

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: One of them would worship a stone, and when he saw one finer than it, he would say: This is finer than that — and he would worship it.
And al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said concerning His saying ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾: The hypocrite, when he desires something, he goes after it.
Then He said: ﴿وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ﴿عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾: He already knew it of him.
And it is said: ﴿عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾ [i.e. while he knew] that it neither benefits him nor harms him.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَآ إِلاَّ ٱلدَّهْرُ﴾.
It may be asked: They do not affirm the Resurrection, so what is the meaning of ﴿نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا﴾?
There are three answers to this:
1- Among them: that the meaning is: some of us die and some live.
2- And among them: that the speech has [a word] put forward and [another] put back (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), and that the meaning is: we live and we die.
3- And the third answer: that the meaning of ﴿نَمُوتُ﴾ is: we are created lifeless, then we live in this world.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَآ إِلاَّ ٱلدَّهْرُ﴾:
Mujāhid said: that is, time, i.e. the passing of the years and the days.
And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: (Do not revile al-dahr (time), for Allah is al-dahr).
There are three views on its meaning:
1- Among them: that the meaning is: do not revile one of the creations of Allah over something in which it has no fault, "for Allah is al-dahr", i.e. the Creator of time — as the Exalted said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with the muḍāf omitted].
2- And it is said: since they used to say "Allah did [such] by time", for it has done such-and-such to us, while it was Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, who decreed those things, He said to them: do not revile the Doer of things, for time does not do them.
3- And it has been related as (for Allah is al-dahra) [with al-dahr in the accusative], and the meaning according to it is: do not revile time, for Allah is abiding throughout time, i.e. abiding forever, never ceasing.
And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾, that he said: [it refers to] their saying "we will not be resurrected".

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً كُلُّ أمَّةٍ تُدْعَىٰ إِلَىٰ كِتَابِهَا﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
Warqāʾ related from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid — and Ibn ʿUyayna from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid — concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً﴾: he said: mustawfirīn upon the knees. «[Translator's note: the printed text has مُسْتَوْفِرِينَ; the following line discusses al-mustawfiz, "one poised/crouching ready to rise", which is evidently the intended word.]»
Mujāhid said — in the narration of Ibn Abī Najīḥ — al-umma here means the single individual.
Sufyān ibn Abī ʿUyayna said: And the mustawfiz is only one [resting] on his knees and the tips of his toes. «[Translator's note: the text reads "Sufyān ibn Abī ʿUyayna"; the well-known name is Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna.]»
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿جَاثِيَةً﴾: at the reckoning.
So this is one view.
And al-Farrāʾ said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً﴾: the people of every religion; and jāthiya: gathered together.
Abū Jaʿfar said: A heap of earth may be called a juthwa, and I reckon al-Farrāʾ took it from this. The poet said:
تَرَى جُثْوتَيْنِ مِنْ تُرَابٍ عَلَيْهِمَا * صَفَائِحُ صُمٌّ مِنْ صَفِيدٍ مُنَضَّدِ
(You see two heaps of earth, upon them solid slabs of stone laid one upon another.)
And the first view is better known and more widespread.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ أمَّةٍ تُدْعَىٰ إِلَىٰ كِتَابِهَا﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that its book is what was prescribed for it of the lawful and the unlawful.
And the other view: that its book is what the angels recorded against it.
And this is more appropriate, because what comes after it points to it.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا كِتَابُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
﴿يَنطِقُ﴾ means: it makes clear.
That is, you look and so you remember what you did.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that the meaning is what the angels write and copy of the deeds of the children of Adam.
And the other view was related by Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has finished [decreeing] what is to be, and the angels copy what will be done, day by day, from the Preserved Tablet; then what the human being does is compared with it, not exceeding that nor falling short.
He said: So it was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: We only supposed that they write it after it is done. He said: You are an Arab people, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ﴾, and copying (istinsākh) can only be from an [existing] copy.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ لآيَاتٍ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
And the meaning is: indeed in the creation of the heavens and the earth.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنتُمْ قَوْماً مُّجْرِمِينَ﴾.
There is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech, and the meaning is: then it will be said to them: Were not My verses recited to you?

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقِيلَ ٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَاكُمْ كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَـٰذَا﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: So today We leave you, just as you left the meeting of this Day of yours.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to this is: so today We leave you in the Fire, just as you left off working for this Day of yours.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَهُوَ ٱلْعِزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾.
al-Kibriyāʾ: grandeur.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾ points to it.
And everything in which there is a spirit is a dābba (creature).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَصْرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَاحِ آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: If He wills, He makes them a mercy, and if He wills, He makes them a punishment.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
That is, after the Qurʾān of Allah [Translator's note: with the muḍāf omitted], as the Exalted said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ﴾.
al-Affāk: the great liar.

safi-cedvel:1-2.t:
* I'rab:
(تنزيل) a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject); (من الله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «تنزيل الكتاب من الله ...» has no grammatical position: inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).

safi-cedvel:3-5.t:
* I'rab:
(في السموات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) for emphasis; (للمؤمنين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.
The clause «إنّ في السموات ... لآيات» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
4- (الواو) conjunction in both places; (في خلقكم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (آيات); (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to خلقكم with a muḍāf implied, i.e. the creation of what He disperses; (من دابة) a tamyīz (specification) of ما — or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied resumptive pronoun —; (لقوم) attached to a naʿt of آيات ...
The clause «في خلقكم ... آيات» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يبثّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يوقنون» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of قوم.
5- (الواو) conjunction in all four places; (اختلاف) genitive by an omitted preposition indicated by the preceding preposition (في), attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ آيات [Note: Or conjoined to خلقكم.. and likewise آيات is conjoined to the first آيات, and there is no new clause in the speech.]; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined to اختلاف by the wāw; (من السماء) attached to (أنزل); (من رزق) attached to (أنزل) [Note: The first (من) is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) and the second (من) is explicative (bayān), so it may validly be attached to a ḥāl of the implied resumptive pronoun.]; (الفاء) conjunction; (به) attached to (أحيا); (بعد) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (أحيا); conjoined to اختلاف, genitive [Translator's note: this phrase stands detached in the source, apparently referring to تصريف الرياح.]; (لقوم) attached to a naʿt of آيات.
The clause «(في) اختلاف الليل ... آيات» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause في خلقكم ... آيات.
The clause «أنزل الله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «أحيا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزل.
The clause «يعقلون» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of the (second) قوم.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(تلك) a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is the clause نتلوها [Note: The khabar may be (آيات), and the clause نتلوها a second khabar or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of آيات, the governing factor in it being the demonstrative, by analogy with the words of Allah the Exalted: «وتلك بيوتهم خاوية» with خاوية in the accusative.]; (عليك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نتلوها); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of نتلو or of its object; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (بأيّ) attached to (يؤمنون), and the interrogative carries the sense of denial; (بعد) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to (يؤمنون) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. after the discourse of Allah.
The clause «تلك آيات الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نتلوها ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ تلك.
The clause «يؤمنون» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if they do not believe in this discourse, then in what discourse will they believe?

safi-cedvel:7-10.t:
* I'rab:
(ويل) a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun was permitted because the word indicates blame.]; (لكلّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) ...
The clause «ويل لكلّ أفّاك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
8- (عليه) attached to (تتلى); (كأن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the effect to the cause; (بعذاب) attached to (بشره).
The clause «يسمع ...» is in the position of genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of أفّاك.
The clause «تتلى ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of آيات.
The clause «يصرّ ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يسمع.
The clause «كأن لم يسمعها» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of يصرّ.
The clause «لم يسمعها» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the lightened كأن.
The clause «بشّره» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: take heed, and give him tidings.
9- (الواو) conjunction; (من آياتنا) attached to a ḥāl of (شيئا); (هزوا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by اتّخذ; (لهم) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب).
The clause «علم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اتّخذها ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أولئك لهم عذاب» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم عذاب» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
10- (من ورائهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ جهنم; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (عنهم) attached to (يغني); (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle in both places; (شيئا) object of يغني [Note: Or a relative noun in both, in the position of nominative, the resumptive pronoun being omitted in both. — A mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. any of availing, the mafʿūl bihi being implied.] [Translator's note: the footnote in the source appears to combine two separate notes, one on (ما) and one on (شيئا).]; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبوا) is in the position of nominative as fāʿil of يغني, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما اتّخذوا) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first maṣdar; (من دون) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi governed by اتّخذوا; (الواو) conjunction; (لهم عذاب عظيم) like لهم عذاب مهين (in the previous verse).
The clause «من ورائهم جهنّم» is in the position of nominative as badal (substitute) of (لهم عذاب ...).
The clause «لا يغني عنهم ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم عذاب.
The clause «كسبوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the first particle-relative (ما).
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first clause لهم عذاب.

* Rhetoric:
Al-taḍādd (a word bearing opposite meanings): in the words of Allah the Exalted «مِنْ وَرائِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ».
Al-taḍādd is the use of a word that admits a meaning and its opposite, being shared between the two meanings, so that it is used for a thing and its opposite.
In this noble verse the figure of taḍādd is found, because the meaning is either "in front of them", since they are heading towards what has been prepared for them, or "behind them", since they are turning away from that and devoting themselves to this world; for وراء is a name for the direction that a person conceals, whether behind or in front.

* Benefits:
- The lightened كأن.
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها. (كأن) is lightened from the heavy form and has governed like إنّ: its noun is the pronoun of the matter, and the clause (لم يسمعها) is in the position of nominative as khabar of كأن. The implied form is (كأنه لم يسمعها). However, its noun may be present and its khabar a single word. The following verse was narrated:
ويوما توافينا بوجه مقسم ... كأن ظبية تعطو إلى وارق السلم
(And one day she meets us with a lovely face, as though a gazelle stretching towards a leafy salam tree.)
with (ظبية) in the accusative as the noun of كأن, the clause after it being an adjective of it and the khabar omitted, the implied form being: as though a stretching gazelle were this woman — by reversed simile, which is more eloquent; with (ظبية) in the nominative as the khabar, the clause after it being an adjective and its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter, the implied form being (كأنها ظبية); and with (ظبية) in the genitive on the view that أن is redundant between the kāf and its genitive noun, the implied form being (كظبية).
When its noun is omitted and its khabar is a nominal clause, it needs no separator, as in the saying of the poet:
ووجه مشرق اللون ... كأن ثدياه حقان
(And a face of radiant colour, as though her breasts were two small round boxes.)
The point of evidence is his saying (كأن ثدياه حقان), where the noun of كأن is the pronoun of the matter, and the clause (ثدياه حقان), made of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, is in the position of nominative as the khabar of كأن, the implied form being (كأنه ثدياه حقان). Therefore there is no separation between كأن and its khabar that is a clause.
But if the khabar is a verbal clause, it is separated by (قد), as in his saying:
لا يهولنّك اصطلاء لظى الحر ... ب فمحذورها كأن قد ألما
(Let not the warming at the blaze of war frighten you, for what is feared of it is as though it had already struck.)
The point of evidence is his saying (كأن قد ألما), where the khabar of كأن is a verbal clause, so it is separated from (كأن) by قد.
Or the separator is (لم), as in the words of Allah the Exalted (كأن لم تغن بالأمس), and the words of Allah the Exalted occurring in the verse under discussion (كأن لم يسمعها).

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(بآيات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كفروا); (لهم عذاب) like the previous one [Note: In verse (9) of the sura.]; (من رجز) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب) ...
The clause «هذا هدى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «الذين كفروا لهم عذاب» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذين).

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سخّر); (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (تجري) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (فيه) attached to (تجري); (بأمره) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الفلك ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تجري ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (سخّر); (الواو) conjunction; (لتبتغوا) like لتجري; (من فضله) attached to (تبتغوا). The interpreted maṣdar (لتبتغوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (سخّر), so it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first maṣdar.
The clause «الله الذي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «تجري ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تبتغوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «لعلّكم تشكرون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), i.e.: that you may be provided for and that you may give thanks.
The clause «تشكرون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.
13- (الواو) conjunction in both places; (لكم) like the first; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (ما) like the first and conjoined to it; (في الأرض) like في السموات; (جميعا) a tawkīd (emphasis) in meaning (maʿnawī) of (ما) [Note: Or it is a ḥāl of (ما في السموات وما في الأرض).]; (منه) attached to a ḥāl of ما [Note: It may be a naʿt (adjective) of (جميعا).]; (في ذلك) attached to a fronted khabar of (إنّ); (اللام) for emphasis; (لقوم) attached to a naʿt of (آيات) ...
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the (first) clause سخّر.
The clause «يتفكّرون ...» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of قوم.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قل); (يغفروا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the answer to the command; the second (للذين) attached to (يغفروا); (لا) negative; (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (يجزي) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزي..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an implied verb, i.e. forgive ... [Note: Or attached to (قل).]
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا..) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يجزي).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يغفروا ...» [Translator's note: the source misprints it as «بغفروا».] has no grammatical position: apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with fāʾ, i.e.: if you say to them "forgive", they will forgive ... so the clause that is the object of speech is implied, i.e. "forgive".
The clause «لا يرجون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يجزي ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «يكسبون» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in the words of Allah the Exalted «لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْماً بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ».
What is meant by "a people" is the believers, who are definite (known); the indefiniteness is for praising and extolling them, i.e. they were commanded to do that so that He may recompense on the Day of Resurrection a people — and what a people! — a people singled out for what they earned in this world of good deeds, among which are patience in the face of the harm of the disbelievers, and overlooking them by restraining anger and bearing what is disliked, [with] such immense reward as words fall short of describing.

* Benefits:
- The words of Allah the Exalted: (قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ), i.e. they do not fear the punitive events of Allah and are heedless of His wrath. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; that was because a man of Banū Ghifār insulted him, and ʿUmar was about to strike him, so Allah revealed this verse and commanded him to pardon him. It is also said: it was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the people of Mecca, who were suffering severe harm from the polytheists before they were commanded to fight; they complained of that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed this verse, and then abrogated it with the verse of fighting.

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (صالحا) an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its adjective, i.e. a righteous deed.]; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (لنفسه) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "عمله"; (الواو) conjunction; (من أساء فعليها) like من عمل.. فلنفسه; (إلى ربّكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb (ترجعون).
The clause «من عمل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عمل صالحا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «(عمله) لنفسه ...» is in the position of jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with fāʾ.
The clause «من أساء ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أساء ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إساءته عليها» is in the position of jussive as apodosis, joined with fāʾ.
The clause «ترجعون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Benefits:
- In this verse there is evidence for the omission of the mubtadaʾ after the fāʾ of the apodosis, in the words of Allah the Exalted (مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَساءَ فَعَلَيْها); the implied forms are (فعمله لنفسه) and (فإساءته عليها).
This discussion has come in detail in Sūrat Fuṣṣilat, verse (49), so go back to it once more.

safi-cedvel:16-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (الكتاب) an accusative second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunction in all four places; (من الطيّبات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رزقناهم); (على العالمين) attached to (فضّلناهم).
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the implied oath ... the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause آتينا.
The clause «فضّلناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتينا.
17- (الواو) conjunction; (من الأمر) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (بيّنات); (الفاء) conjunction; (ما) negative; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (من بعد) attached to (اختلفوا); (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (بغيا) an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) [Note: Or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb.]; (بينهم) an accusative adverb (ẓarf), attached to a naʿt of (بغيا). The interpreted maṣdar (ما جاءهم ...) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The second (بينهم) is attached to (يقضي); (يوم) an accusative adverb of time, attached to (يقضي); (في ما) attached to (يقضي); (فيه) attached to (يختلفون).
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتينا.
The clause «اختلفوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتينا.
The clause «جاءهم العلم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ ربّك يقضي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقضي ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «كانوا فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يختلفون» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كانوا.
18- (ثمّ) for conjunction — or resumptive —; (على شريعة) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (من الأمر) attached to a naʿt of (شريعة); (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the cause to the effect; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making jussive, and the second is negative ...
The clause «جعلناك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the oath [Note: Or originally resumptive, according to the meaning.].
The clause «اتّبعها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to a resumption caused by what preceded, i.e.: take heed, and follow it.
The clause «لا تتبع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اتّبعها.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
19- (عنك) attached to (يغنوا) by its being made to carry the meaning of يدفعوا "repel" (taḍmīn); (من الله) attached to a ḥāl of (شيئا) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from the punishment of Allah; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (بعضهم) a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is (أولياء).
The clause «إنّهم لن يغنوا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the preceding prohibition.
The clause «لن يغنوا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ الظالمين ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.
The clause «بعضهم أولياء ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the (second) إنّ.
The clause «الله وليّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.
20- (للناس) attached to a naʿt of (بصائر); (لقوم) attached to (رحمة).
The clause «هذا بصائر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يوقنون» is in the position of genitive as naʿt of قوم.

* Morphology:
(18) شريعة: a name for the water that people come down to drink; its plural is شرائع. Then it was borrowed for religion.. or it is a name for a doctrine and creed (milla); its pattern is فعيلة with fatḥa then kasra.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
His saying: {تَنزِيلُ}: the like of this has been given earlier, at the beginning of Ghāfir. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: "If «العزيزِ الحكيمِ» are two attributes of Allah, then it is literal; if they are two attributes of the Book, then it is figurative." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected his making them two attributes of the Book, saying: "For if it were so, the attribute would directly follow the thing it describes, and one would say: 'the revelation of the mighty, wise Book from Allah.'" He said: "Because «من الله», if it is attached to «تَنْزيل», and «تنزيل» is the khabar of «حم» or of an omitted mubtadaʾ, then it would necessarily separate the attribute from the thing described, and that is not permitted, just as it is not permitted to say 'the striking of Zayd with a whip, the excellent, pleased me'; or if it is in the position of the khabar, with «تنزيلُ» as mubtadaʾ, then separation by it is likewise not permitted, as it is not permitted to say: 'the striking of Zayd is severe, the excellent.'"

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٍ}: there are two aspects to it. The more apparent: it is conjoined to «خَلْقِكم», which is genitive through «في», the implied form being "and in what He scatters." The second: it is conjoined to the pronoun that is genitive through «الخَلْق», according to the school of those who permit conjunction upon a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition. al-Zamakhsharī considered it ugly even if emphasis is added, as in "I passed by you yourself and Zayd." By this he points to the school of al-Jarmī, who says: if emphasis is added it is permitted, otherwise not; so his saying is a third school.
His saying: {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ} and {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ}: the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «آياتٍ» with kasra in both places, and the others read both with nominative. There is no disagreement about the kasra of the first, because it is the ism of «إنَّ». As for {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ} with kasra, two aspects are possible. The first: it is conjoined to the ism of «إنَّ», and the khabar is His saying «وفي خَلْقِكم». It is as if it were said: "and in your creation and in what He scatters of creatures are signs." The second: it is repeated for emphasis of the first «آيات», and «في خَلْقكم» is conjoined to «في السماوات», the preposition having been repeated with it for emphasis. A parallel is your saying: "Indeed in your house is Zayd, and in the market Zayd": the second «زيداً» is emphasis of the first, as if you had said "indeed Zayd, Zayd, is in your house and in the market"; and in this there is no conjunction upon the objects of two operators at all.
Abū l-Baqāʾ erred by counting it among those, saying: "{آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ} is read with kasra on the tāʾ, and there are two aspects to it. The first: an «إنَّ» is implied, omitted on the evidence of the first «إنَّ»; and «آيات» is not conjoined to the first «آيات», because that would be conjunction upon the objects of two operators. The second: it is repeated for emphasis, because it is of the same word as the first «آيات»; and its i'rab is like your saying: 'There is blood on your garment and on Zayd's garment, blood': the second 'blood' is a repetition, because you could do without mentioning it." End of quotation.
His saying "it is not conjoined to the first «آيات» because that would be conjunction upon two operators" is an error; where is the object of the other operator? It is as if he imagined that «في» had dropped out of His saying «وفي خَلْقِكم», or he confused {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ} with this one; for in that one there is something that suggests conjunction upon two operators, which he himself also mentioned.
As for the nominative, it too has two aspects. The first: «في خَلْقِكم» is a fronted khabar and «آياتٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ, a clause conjoined to a clause emphasised by «إنَّ». The second: it is conjoined to the first «آيات» according to position, by the view of those who permit that, especially those who say it is permitted after the khabar by consensus.
As for His saying {واختلاف الليل والنهار} (the verse): you have learned that the two companions read «آيات» with kasra, and this needs clarification, for people have spoken at length about it and have derived several different aspects for it, and it has been cited as proof that conjunction upon two operators is permitted.
I say: conjunction upon two operators is not specific to the reading of the two companions; it can also be cited from the reading of the others, as you will see, if Allah the Exalted wills. As for the reading of the two companions, it has several aspects. The first: «اختلافِ الليلِ» is genitive through an implied «في», omitted because it has been mentioned twice before; and a preposition, when there is evidence for it, may be omitted while its operation is retained. Sībawayh recited:
4023 - الآن قَرَّبْتَ تَهْجُونا وتَشْتِمُنا ... فاذهَبْ فما بك والأيامِ من عَجَبِ
(Now you have come close to lampooning and insulting us; so go, for there is nothing strange about you and the days.)
Its implied form is "and in the days," because the bāʾ preceded in «بك»; and it cannot be conjoined to the kāf, because it is not Sībawayh's school, as you know, to conjoin to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition. So the implied form in this verse is "and in the alternation are signs," with «آيات» following the two aspects mentioned earlier for the «آيات» before it: conjunction or emphasis. They said: what indicates this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), «وفي اختلافِ», stating «في» explicitly. These are two aspects.
The third: «اختلافِ» is conjoined to what is genitive through «في», and «آياتٍ» to what is accusative through «إنَّ». This is conjunction upon two operators, and its verification is conjunction upon the objects of two operators: you conjoined «اختلاف» to «خَلْق», which is genitive through «في», so it is the object of one operator, and you conjoined «آياتٍ» to the ism of «إنَّ», which is the object of another operator; thus with one particle, the wāw, you conjoined two objects, «اختلاف» and «آيات», to the two objects before them, namely «خَلْق» and «آيات». From its apparent sense those who permit this have drawn proof, such as al-Akhfash. There are four schools on the question: prohibition absolutely, which is the school of Sībawayh and the majority of the Basrans. They said: because it leads to the conjunction particle standing in the place of two operators, which is not permitted, for if it were permitted for two it would be permitted for three, and no one says so; and because the conjunction particle is weak and has no strength to deputise for two operators; and because the one who says it is permitted considers it weak, and the better view according to him is that it is not permitted, so the Book of Allah should not be carried onto it; and because it is like transitivity through two transitivisers by one transitiviser, which is not permitted.
Ibn al-Sarrāj said: "Conjunction upon two operators is an error in analogy and is not heard from the Arabs." Then he took what is in this verse as repetition for emphasis. al-Rummānī said: "It is like your saying: 'Indeed in the house is Zayd and in the room Zayd,' which is permitted by consensus. So reflect on this aspect that Ibn al-Sarrāj mentioned, for it is very good, and the Book of Allah must be carried only onto it. I have explained the reading with kasra, and there is no fault in it in the Qur'an on any aspect, whereas conjunction upon two operators is a fault according to both those who permit it and those who do not, so it has reached the extreme of fault; thus this verse may be carried only onto what Ibn al-Sarrāj mentioned, and not onto what others have held."
I say: this restriction by him is not conceded, for the verse has other derivations besides what Ibn al-Sarrāj mentioned, which it is permissible to carry it onto. al-Zajjāj said: "And the like of it in poetry:
4024 - أكلَّ امرِئٍ تَحْسَبين امْرَأً ... ونارٍ تَوَقَّدُ بالليلِ نارا
(Do you reckon every man a man, and every fire that burns at night a fire?)
al-Fārisī recited for al-Farazdaq:
4025 - وباشَرَ راعيها الصَّلا بلَبانِه ... وجَنْبَيْه حَرَّ النارِ ما يتحرَّق
(Its herdsman faced the fire with his chest, and with his two sides the heat of the fire, without burning.)
and the saying of another:
4026 - أَوْصَيْتُ مِنْ رُبْدَةَ قَلْباً حُرَّاً ... بالكلبِ خيراً والحَماةِ شَرا
(I charged, on behalf of Rubda, a free heart: kindness to the dog, and harshness to the mother-in-law.)
I say: as for the first verse, its apparent sense is that he conjoined «نارٍ» to «امرئ», which is genitive through «كل», and the second «ناراً» to the second «امرَأً». The implied form is "and you reckon every fire a fire"; thus he conjoined upon the objects of two operators. In the second verse he conjoined «جَنْبَيْه» to «بلبانه», and conjoined «حَرَّ النارِ» to «الصلا»; the implied form is "and he faced the heat of the fire with his two sides." In the third verse he conjoined «الحَماة» to «الكلب» and «شَرًّا» to «خيراً», its implied form being "and I charged kindness to the mother-in-law, harshness." In all of that Sībawayh holds the genitive to be by an implied genitive-governing preposition, but this is objected to on the ground that the operation of an implied preposition is very weak; do you not see that "I passed Zayd," with Zayd genitive, is not permitted except in necessity, as in the saying:
4027 - إذا قيلَ أيُّ الناسِ شرُّ قبيلةٍ ... أشارَتْ كليبٍ بالأكفِّ الأصابعُ
(When it is asked which people is the worst tribe, the fingers point with palms to Kulayb.)
meaning "to Kulayb"; and the saying of another:
4028 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... حتى تَبَذَّخَ فارتقى الأعلامِ
meaning "to the landmarks." So he fled from one thing and fell into something weaker. It is answered: since the preposition has already been mentioned in the wording, the indication of it is strong, so it is as if it were pronounced, unlike what you cited in the example and the poetry.
The second school: the detailed view, which is the school of al-Akhfash. It is permitted on two conditions. The first: that one of the two operators be a preposition. The second: that the conjoined element be adjacent to the conjunction particle or be separated by «لا». An example of the first is the noble verse and the verses I gave earlier. Therefore al-Mubarrad judged his citing the verse as proof sound. An example of separation by «لا» is your saying: "Zayd is not in the house, nor Amr in the room." If both conditions are missing, such as: "Indeed/ Zayd insulted Bishr, and by Allah Khālid Hind," or if one is missing, such as: "Indeed Zayd struck Bakr, and Khālid Bishr," Ibn Mālik reported prohibition according to everyone. There is something to consider in that, given the disagreement you will learn of.
The third: it is permitted on condition that one of the two operators is a preposition and that it is the earlier one, like the noble verse; if it did not come first, like "Indeed Zayd is in the house, and Amr the market," it is not permitted, and likewise if it were not a preposition, as exemplified earlier.
The fourth: permission, which is attributed to al-Farrāʾ.
The fourth aspect among the derivations of the reading mentioned: that «آيات» is accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it will come in what I relate from him.
As for the nominative reading, it has several aspects. The first and second are what preceded under {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ}. The third: that it is emphasis of the «آيات» before it, as it was in the accusative reading. The fourth: that the question is of the chapter of conjunction upon two operators; for «اختلافِ» is conjoined to «خَلْقِكم», which is the object of «في», and «آيات» is conjoined to the «آيات» before it, which is the object of the inceptive (ibtidāʾ); so in this reading too he conjoined upon the objects of two operators. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is read {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ} with nominative and accusative, on the pattern of your saying: 'Indeed Zayd is in the house and Amr in the market,' or 'and Amr is in the market.' As for His saying {آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ}, it is of the conjunction upon two operators whether you make it accusative or nominative. The two operators in the accusative are «إنَّ» and «في»; the wāw was placed in their stead, so it effected the genitive in {واختلاف اليل والنهار} and the accusative in «آياتٍ». If you make it nominative, the two operators are the inceptive and «في»; it effected the nominative in «آيات» and the genitive in «اختلاف»." Then he said, in justifying the accusative: "And the second is that it is accusative as specification after the genitive phrase is completed."
The fifth aspect: «آياتٌ» is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are signs." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) took issue with him and said: "Attributing the genitive and nominative, and the genitive and accusative, to the wāw is not correct, because the sound view among the schools is that the conjunction particle does not operate." I say: Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma also took issue with him, saying: "Some of them say: on this reading too, meaning the nominative reading, it is conjunction upon two operators, namely the particle «في» and the inceptive that requires the nominative. And some of them do not use this expression for this reading, because the inceptive is not a verbal operator."
It was also read «واختلافُ» nominative with «آيةٌ» nominative and singular, as mubtadaʾ and khabar, and likewise {وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٌ آيةٌ} was read in the singular. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa and ʿĪsā read «وتصريف الريح»; so the Shaykh said. I say: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī also read with this reading, and that was given earlier in Sūrat al-Baqara.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {نَتْلُوهَا}: it may be the khabar of «تلك», with «آيات الله» a badal or ʿaṭf bayān. It may also be that «تلك آيات» is mubtadaʾ and khabar, with «نَتْلُوها» a ḥāl. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The operator is what «تلك» indicates of the sense of pointing, like {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72]." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "It is not like it, because in {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72] there is a particle of attention (ha). It is said that the operator in the ḥāl is what the particle of attention indicates, i.e. 'pay attention.' As for «تلك», it has no particle of attention; if the particle of attention operates by what it contains of the sense of drawing attention, since a particle may operate in the ḥāl, then the meaning is: 'pay attention to Zayd in the state of his old age' or 'in the state of his standing.' It is also said that the operator in a construction like this is an omitted verb that the meaning indicates, i.e. 'look at him in the state of his old age,' and the demonstrative is not an operator, nor is the particle of attention, if there is one."
I say: rather, the verse is like {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72] in respect of attributing the operation to the demonstrative. The most that can be said is that the other verse contains something fit to be an operator, and this does not undermine the comparison when you intend a shared aspect. As for implying a verb, it is shared in both places by those who hold that view. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In «نتْلوها» there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'we recite their matter and the explanation of the lesson in them.' It is also possible that by 'the signs of Allah' he means the Qur'an sent down in this sense, so there is no omitted muḍāf in it." / Some read «يَتْلوها» with the third-person yāʾ, referring back to the Creator, the Exalted. «بالحَقِّ» is a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "joined to the truth," and from the object, i.e. "joined to the truth." It may also be causal, and so be attached to «نَتْلوها» itself.
His saying: {بَعْدَ الله وَآيَاتِهِ}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. after the signs of Allah; it is like your saying: 'Zayd and his generosity pleased me,' meaning Zayd's generosity." The Shaykh rejected this: it is not what is meant; rather two things pleasing are meant; and there is in it an intrusion of nouns without necessity. He said: "This is an inversion of the realities of grammar."
The two Ḥaramī readers (Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr), Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «يُؤْمنون» with the third-person yāʾ. The others read it with the second-person tāʾ. His saying «فبأيِّ» is attached to it and is fronted because it has the head of the sentence.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {يَسْمَعُ}: it may be resumptive, i.e. "he hears," either with or without implying «هو»; it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أثيم»; and it may be an adjective.
His saying: «تُتْلَى عليه»: a ḥāl from «آياتِ الله». The disagreement does not arise here, namely that it could be in the position of the accusative as a second object; for the condition of that is that what follows it be something that is not heard, such as "I heard Zayd reciting." But when what follows it is something that is heard, such as "I heard the recitation of Zayd, chanting it," it is transitive to one object only; and the verses are among what is heard.
His saying: «ثم يُصِرُّ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «ثم» in His saying {ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِراً}? I say: as its meaning in the saying of the poet:
4029 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يرى غَمَراتِ الموتِ ثم يزورُها
(He sees the depths of death, then visits them.)
That is because the depths of death deserve that whoever sees them should save himself and seek flight from them, whereas visiting them and advancing to engage them is far-fetched. So the meaning of «ثم» is to signal that the act of one who advances upon them after seeing and beholding them is a thing deemed remote in habits and natures. Likewise the clear signs of Allah, speaking the truth: for whoever has them recited to him and hears them, his persistence in error at them and his arrogance against believing in them is deemed remote in speech."
His saying: {كَأَن لَّمْ يَسْمَعْهَا}: this clause may be resumptive or a ḥāl.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَإِذَا عَلِمَ}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn and kasra on the lām, lightened, active. Qatāda and Maṭar al-Warrāq read «عُلِّم», passive with shadda.
His saying: «اتَّخَذها»: there are two aspects to the feminine pronoun. The first: it refers back to «آياتِنا». The second: it refers back to «شيئاً», although it is masculine, because it has the sense of "sign," like the saying of Abū l-ʿAtāhiya:
4030 - نفْسي بشيءٍ من الدنيا مُعَلَّقَةٌ ... اللَّهُ والقائمُ المهدِيُّ يَقْضِيها
(My soul is attached to something of this world; Allah and the rising Mahdī will fulfil it.)
because by «شيء» he meant a slave-girl called ʿUtba.
His saying: «أولئك»: an indication of the meaning of «كلِّ أَفَّاكٍ»; it was first taken according to its wording, so it was singular, then according to its meaning, so it was pluralised, like His saying: {كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 53].
His saying: {وَلاَ مَا اتخذوا}: conjoined to «ما كَسَبوا». The «ما» in both is either a maṣdar particle or has the sense of "that which," i.e. "their earning will not avail, nor their taking," or "that which they earned, nor that which they took."

semin-durr:11-11.t: And His saying: {مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ}: it has been mentioned in Sabaʾ.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {جَمِيعاً مِّنْهُ}: «جميعاً» is a ḥāl from {مَّا فِي السماوات وَمَا فِي الأرض}, or tawkīd (emphasis). Ibn Mālik counted it among the words of emphasis. «منه» may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «جميعاً», or attached to «سَخَّر», i.e. "it proceeds from His side and from Him." al-Zamakhsharī allowed «منه» to be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "all of it is from Him," and also that {وَمَا فِي الأرض} be a mubtadaʾ and «منه» its khabar. The Shaykh said: "These two are not permitted except by the view of al-Akhfash, in that the ḥāl, in the sense of «جميعاً», has been fronted before its semantic operator, i.e. the preposition, so it is parallel to 'Zayd, standing, is in the house.'" The majority read «مِنْه» as preposition and genitive. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with kasra on the mīm, shadda on the nūn and accusative tāʾ, making it a maṣdar from مَنَّ يَمُنَّ مِنَّةً; so its accusative, in his reading, is as an emphatic maṣdar, either through an implied operator or through «سَخَّر», since it is of its meaning. Abū Ḥātim said: "The chain of this reading back to Ibn ʿAbbās is obscure." I say: it has also been transmitted from a group of eminent men other than Ibn ʿAbbās; Ibn Khālawayh related it from him and from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, and the author of al-Lawāmiḥ and Ibn Jinnī related it from Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, al-Jaḥdarī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.
Maslama ibn Muḥārib read likewise, except that he made the tāʾ nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is from Him." He also read, in another transmission, with fatḥa on the mīm, shadda on the nūn and a pronominal hāʾ with ḍamma, making it a maṣdar annexed to the pronoun of Allah the Exalted.
Its nominative has two aspects: the first, as agent of «سَخَّر», i.e. "His favour upon you subjected these things to you"; the second, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it," or "that is His favour upon you."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ يَغْفِرُواْ}: its parallel has already been given in Sūrat Ibrāhīm.
His saying: «ليَجْزِيَ»: Ibn ʿĀmir and the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «لنجزيَ» with the nūn of majesty, i.e. "that We may recompense." The rest of the seven read «ليجزِيَ» with the yāʾ (below), active, i.e. "that Allah may recompense." Abū Jaʿfar, with a disagreement reported from him, Shayba and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read likewise, except that it is passive. This is with «قوماً» accusative. / As for what stands in the place of the agent there are three aspects. The first: the pronoun of the second object, the pronoun returning to it because the context indicates it, its implied form being "that it may be recompensed, i.e. the good, upon a people." The second object of the «أَعْطى» type stands in the place of the agent without disagreement; a parallel is "the dirham was given to Zayd." The second: what stands in its place is the pronoun of the maṣdar indicated by the verb, i.e. "that the recompense be recompensed." There is something to consider in this, because the direct object is not left and the maṣdar put in its place, especially without its being stated. The third: what stands in its place is the preposition and its genitive noun. In this there is a proof for al-Akhfash and the Kufans, who permit a non-object to deputise while the object is present, and they recited:
4031 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... لَسُبَّ بذلك الجَرْوِ الكِلابا
([…] by that puppy the dogs were reviled.)
and the saying:
4032 - لم يُعْنَ بالعلياءِ إلاَّ سَيِّدا ...
(None cared for the heights except a chief.)
The Basrans do not allow it.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {على شَرِيعَةٍ}: it is the second object of «جَعَلْناك». The sharīʿa originally is the waters that people come down to in rivers. That place is called sharīʿa. The plural is sharāʾiʿ. He said:
4033 - وفي الشَّرائِع مِنْ جَيْلانَ مُقْتَنِصٌ ... رَثُّ الثيابِ خَفِيُّ الشخصِ مُنْسَرِبُ
(And at the watering places of Jaylān is a hunter, in tattered clothes, his form hidden, slipping about.)
That was borrowed for religion, because servants come to what gives their souls life.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {هذا بَصَائِرُ}: i.e. this Qur'an. It is the plural of «بَصيرة», considering what is in it. «هذه» was also read, referring back to the verses, and because the Qur'an is in their sense, like the saying:
4034 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سائِلْ بني أَسَدٍ ما هذه الصَّوْتُ
(Ask the Banū Asad what this noise is.)
because it is in the sense of "the cry" (al-ṣayḥa).

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {أَمْ حَسِبَ}: «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), so it is implied as "rather" and the interrogative hamza, or as "rather" alone, or as the hamza alone. The verification of this has been given.
His saying: {كالذين آمَنُواْ}: it is the second object of the "making," i.e. "that We make them be like those who believed," i.e. they do not reckon that. It was mentioned in Sūrat al-Ḥajj that the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «سواءً» here accusative, and the others nominative, and I promised to discuss it here. So I say, and with Allah is success: as for the accusative reading, there are three aspects to it. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «كالذين آمنوا», and the second object of the making is «كالذين آمنوا», i.e. "Did they reckon that We would make them like them in a state of equality of their life and death? It is not so." The second: «سواءً» is the second object of the making, and «كالذين» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "We will not make them, while being like them, equal"; and its meaning is not that. The third: «سواءً» is a second object of «حَسِب».
Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to this aspect, and I think it a mistake, as will become clear to you. He said: "It is also read accusative. There are two aspects: the first, it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the kāf, i.e. 'We make them like the believers in this state.' The second: it is a second object of «حَسِب», with the kāf a ḥāl, and the equality of their life and death has entered into the reckoning; and on this aspect their life and their death are nominative through «سواء», because it has gained strength by its reliance (on a ḥāl)." End quotation. He has thus stated explicitly that it is a second object of the reckoning. This is not correct at all, because «حَسِبَ» and its sisters, when the doubled «أنَّ», or the lightened «أَنْ», or the subjunctive «أَنْ» occurs after them, stand in for two objects; and here the subjunctive «أنْ» occurs after the reckoning, so it stands in for the two objects; so how could «سواءً» be a second object of «حَسِب»?
If you say: what I have said is the opinion of the majority, Sībawayh and others, but others, like al-Akhfash, claim that it stands in for one; and given this, it is possible that Abū l-Baqāʾ followed this school, so he parsed «أَنْ نجعلَهم» as a first object and «سواءً» as a second object.
The answer: al-Akhfash stated explicitly that the second object is then omitted. And even if we concede that it is not omitted, it is prevented from another aspect: «محياهُم ومماتُهم» are made nominative by it, because it has the sense of "equal," as stated earlier, and there is no pronoun returning from its nominative to the first object; rather it makes nominative something foreign to the first object. This is like: "I reckoned your standing equal, your going and its absence."
As for whoever reads it nominative, his reading admits two aspects: the first, that «سواءٌ» is a fronted khabar and «مَحْياهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ/ and the second, that «سواء» is the mubtadaʾ and «مَحْياهم» its khabar.
So they parsed it. There is something to consider in this, mentioned in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, namely that it is indefinite with nothing to justify it, and whenever a definite and an indefinite meet, one makes the indefinite the khabar, not the mubtadaʾ. Then in this clause there are three aspects. The first: it is resumptive. The second: it is a badal for the kāf that falls as second object. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because a clause may fall as a second object, it is in the ruling of the single word. Do you not see that if you said: 'that We make them equal, their life and their death,' it would be sound, as you say: 'I thought Zayd, his father is departing.'" The Shaykh said: "This, I mean substituting a clause for a single word, was permitted by Ibn Jinnī and Ibn Mālik, and prohibited by Ibn al-ʿIlj," then he mentioned from him much speech in establishing that, then said: "And what appears is that it is not permitted," meaning what al-Zamakhsharī allowed. He said: "Because it has the sense of 'transforming,' and it is not permitted to say 'I made Zayd, his father is standing,' since transformation is a transition from one entity to another, or from a description in the entity to another description in it. And that clause that falls after the object of the implied «صَيَّرْت», as a second object, contains no transition of what we mentioned, so it is not permitted." I say: and one may say: rather, there is in it a transition from a description in the entity to a description in it, because the grammarians stated explicitly that a clause may fall as an adjective and as a ḥāl, as in: "I passed by a man whose father is standing," and "Zayd came, his father standing." So what they judged to be adjectival and circumstantial may fall within the scope of transformation, since there is no difference between one description and another in this respect.
The third: the clause is a ḥāl, the implied form being: "Or do the disbelievers reckon that We will make them like the believers in a state of equality of their life and death? They are not so; rather they are divided." This is the apparent view according to the Shaykh. On the last two aspects the clause falls within the scope of the reckoning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, for he said: "This speech requires that the wording of the verse is a statement, and it appears that His saying {سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ} falls within the denounced, evil reckoning; and this is a good possibility, and the first is fine." End quotation. He did not explain how it enters the reckoning, and the manner is one of the last two aspects: either badal or ḥāl, as you have learned.
al-Aʿmash read «سواءً» accusative with «مَحْياهم ومَماتَهم» also accusative. As for «سواءً», it is a second object or a ḥāl, as stated earlier.
