As for the accusative of «مَحْياهم ومماتَهم», there are two aspects: the first, that they are two adverbs of time, accusative as a badal for the object of «نَجْعَلَهم», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), with «سواءً» in that case being the second object. The implied form: "that We make their life and their death equal." The second: they are accusative as adverbs of time, and the operator is either the making or «سواء». The implied form: "that We make them equal at these two times," or "make them equal at these two times."
al-Zamakhsharī said, implying this aspect: "Whoever reads it accusative makes «مَحْياهم ومماتَهم» two adverbs, like 'the arrival of the pilgrim' and 'the setting of the star.'"
The Shaykh said: "His example of 'the setting of the star' is not good, because «خُفوق» is a maṣdar not on the pattern maf ʿal, so in truth it involves an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'the time of setting,' unlike «مَحْيا», «مَمات» and «مَقْدَم», which are set down as shared among three meanings: maṣdar, time and place. When they are used as maṣdar, that is by original setting, not by omitting a muḍāf like «خُفوق»; for there must be an omitted muḍāf for it, as it is set down as a maṣdar." This is a minor matter, because he only meant that this word occurs with time intended by it. Whether it is by origin or by derivation does not harm.
The pronoun in «مَحْياهم ومماتُهم» may refer back to both groups, meaning: the life and death of the believers are equal with Allah in honour, and the life and death of the wrongdoers are equal in disgrace with Him; so he folded the speech, relying on the listener's mind and understanding. It may also refer back to the wrongdoers only: He reports that their state in the two times is equal.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«مَماتَهم» is also read accusative, i.e. 'in their life and their death.' The operator is «نَجْعل» or «سواء». It is also said it is an adverb." I say: his saying "it is also said" is the first view exactly.
His saying: {سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ}: its parsing has been given. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "«ما» is a maṣdar particle, i.e. 'evil is their judgement.'"

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {بالحق}: three aspects: a ḥāl from the agent, or from the object, or the bāʾ is causal.
His saying: «ولِتُجْزَى»: three aspects. The first: it is conjoined to «بالحق» in meaning, because each of them is a cause; / so a reason was conjoined to its like. The second: it is conjoined to an omitted thing being justified, its implied form being "that He may indicate by them His power, and that every soul be recompensed." The third: it is the lām of consequence, i.e. "and the matter from them became such that a people were guided by them and others went astray from them."

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {أَفَرَأَيْتَ}: in the sense of "tell me," and its ruling has been explained earlier. The first object is «مَنْ اتَّخذ», and the second is omitted, its implied form after «غشاوة» being "will he be guided?", and His saying «فَمَنْ يهْديه» indicates it. I implied it after «غشاوة» only because of the ṣilas of the relative noun.
His saying: «على عِلْمٌ»: a ḥāl from the Majestic Name, i.e. "being, by His knowledge, aware of it, that he is deserving of that." It is also said to be a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "He led him astray while he knew," and this is more heinous for him.
al-Aʿraj read «آلهةً» in the plural, and from him likewise annexed to his pronoun: «آلهتَه هواه».
His saying: «غِشاوة»: the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «غَشْوَة» with fatḥa on the ghayn and sukūn on the shīn. al-Aʿmash and Ibn Muṣarrif likewise, except that they put kasra on the ghayn. The rest of the seven read «غِشاوة» with kasra on the ghayn. Ibn Masʿūd and also al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa, which is the dialect of Rabīʿa. al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima and ʿAbd Allāh also read it with ḍamma, which is the dialect of ʿUkl. The discussion of that was given at the beginning of al-Baqara, and that it was read there with the undotted ʿayn. The majority read «تَذَكَّرون» with shadda; al-Jaḥdarī lightened it. al-Aʿmash read it with two tāʾs, «تَتَذَكَّرون».
His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ الله}: i.e. after Allah's leading him astray.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {وَقَالُواْ مَا هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا}: the parallel of all these verses has been given. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نُحْيا» with ḍamma on the nūn.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ}: the majority read «الحجة» accusative. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read it nominative, and the interpretation of that has been given. «ما كان» is the apodosis of the conditional «إذا». The Shaykh made it evidence for the apodosis of «إذا» not operating in it, because what follows «ما» does not operate on what precedes it. He said: "It differs from the other conditional particles, in that the fāʾ is not joined to its apodosis when it is negated with «ما»."

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ}: there are two aspects regarding its operator. The first: it is «يَخْسَرُ», and «يومئذٍ» is a badal from «يومَ تَقومُ»; the tanwīn on this view is a tanwīn of compensation for an implied clause, and no clause has preceded except «تقومُ الساعةُ», so the implied form becomes "and on the day the Hour arises, on that day the Hour arises." What they implied has no added benefit, so it is an emphatic badal. The second: its operator is implied. They said: because the Day of Resurrection is a third state, neither the heaven nor the earth, since those two are replaced; so it is as if it were said: "To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and the dominion on the day the Hour arises." And His saying «يومئذ» is then governed by «يَخْسَرُ». The clause is resumptive in wording, though it has a connection with what precedes it in meaning.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {جَاثِيَةً}: a ḥāl, because the apparent view is that the seeing is visual. The jāthiya is the one on the knees, because it is fearful, and the sinner is on the verge of rising. It is also said: gathered together; from it comes الجُثْوَة for a grave, because of the stones gathered on it. He said:
4035 - تَرَى جُثْوَتَيْنِ مِنْ تُرابٍ عليهما ... صَفائِحٌ صُمٌّ مِنْ صَفِيْحٍ مُنَضَّدِ
(You see two mounds of earth with solid slabs upon them, of stacked flat stone.)
It was also read «جاذِيَةً» with dotted dhāl, which is more intensely on the verge of rising than the jāthī.
His saying: «كلُّ أمةٍ»: the majority read it nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «تُدْعى» its khabar. Yaʿqūb read it accusative as a badal from the first «كُلُّ أمة», a badal of a described indefinite from its like.
His saying: «اليومَ تُجْزَوْن»: this clause is governed by an implied saying, the implied form being "it is said to them: today you are recompensed." «اليومَ» is governed by what follows it, and «وما كُنتم» is the second object.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {يَنطِقُ}: it may be a ḥāl, or a second khabar, or «كتابُنا» may be a badal and «يَنْطِقُ» the khabar by itself. And «بالحق» is a ḥāl.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {أَفَلَمْ}: it too is upon an implied saying. al-Zamakhsharī, by his habit, implied a clause between the hamza and the fāʾ, i.e. "Did My messengers not come to you, and My signs were not…"

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ وعْدَ الله}: the majority read it with kasra on the hamza, because it is quoted by the saying. al-Aʿraj and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read it with fatḥa. That is derived from the dialect of Sulaym: they treat "say" like "think" absolutely. In it is the saying:
4036 - إذا قلتُ أنِّي آيِبٌ أهلَ بلدةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I said that I was returning to the people of a town… )
His saying: «والساعةُ»: Ḥamza read it accusative, conjoined to «وعدَ الله». The others read it nominative, and there are three aspects: the inceptive, with the negated clause that follows as its khabar. The second: conjunction upon the position of the ism of «إنَّ», because/ before it enters it is nominative through the inceptive. The third: conjunction upon the position of «إنَّ» and its ism together, because some, such as al-Fārisī and al-Zamakhsharī, hold that «إنَّ» and its ism have a position, which is the nominative through the inceptive.
His saying: «إلاَّ ظَنَّاً»: this verse needs an interpretation. That is because it is permitted to free the operator for what follows it from all its governed words, whether nominative or not, except the absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), for it is not freed for it. It is not permitted to say "You struck nothing except a striking," as if there is no benefit in it; that is because it is like repetition of the verb, so it is as if equivalent to "I struck nothing except I struck." This reason had occurred to me until I saw Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ inclining to it, so praise be to Allah.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «إنْ نَظُنُّ إلاَّ ظَنًّا»? I say: its origin is 'we think a thinking,' and its meaning is the affirmation of thinking only. So he brought in the negation particle and the exception so as to convey the affirmation of thinking and the negation of anything besides it; and the negation of anything besides thinking was increased for emphasis by His saying {وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ}." The apparent sense of his speech is that he does not interpret the verse but takes it according to its apparent sense; therefore the Shaykh said: "This is the speech of one with no awareness of the grammatical rule, namely that freeing applies to all governed words, agent, object and others, except the emphatic maṣdar, which does not admit it."
People have differed in interpreting it, on several aspects. The first: what al-Mubarrad said, namely that the original is "we are nothing but ones who think a thinking." He said: "A parallel is what Abū ʿAmr related: 'The perfume is nothing but musk,' its implied form: 'there is nothing but the perfume, musk.'" I say: he means that the ism of «ليس» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) latent in it, and «إلاَّ الطيبُ المسكُ» is in the position of the accusative as its khabar; and it seems it escaped him that the dialect of Tamīm is to cancel the operation of «ليس» when its negation is broken by «إلاَّ», by analogy with the Hijazi «ما»; the question is long and is mentioned in my book "Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl," and an anecdote related to it passed between Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar. The second: «ظنَّاً» has an omitted adjective, its implied form being "except a clear thinking," so it is specifying, not emphatic. The third: «نظنُّ» is made to contain the sense of "we believe," so «ظنَّاً» is accusative as a direct object, not a maṣdar. The fourth: the original is "we do not think except that you think a thinking," and all this was omitted; it is also attributed to al-Mubarrad. They rejected it against him, in that he omitted «أنَّ», its ism and its khabar, and left the maṣdar. This is not permitted. The fifth: thinking (ẓann) may have the sense of knowledge and of doubt, so he excepted doubt, as if it were said: "We have no belief except doubt." Like the verse is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
4037 - وحَلَّ به الشَّيْبُ أثقالَه ... وما اعْتَرَّه الشيبُ إلاَّ اعْتِرارا
(Grey hair settled its burdens on him, and grey hair came upon him nothing but a coming upon.)
He means a clear coming upon.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا}: an instance of latitude in the adverb of time, in that he annexed to it what occurs within it, like {بَلْ مَكْرُ اليل والنهار} [Sabaʾ: 33]. The disagreement over His saying «لا يُخْرَجُون» was given at the beginning of al-Aʿrāf. The meaning of istiʿtāb (seeking to be satisfied) was also given.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {رَبِّ السماوت وَرَبِّ الأرض رَبِّ العالمين}: the majority read «ربِّ» in all three as genitive, following the Majestic Name, as explicative apposition, badal or adjective. Ibn Muḥayṣin read all three as nominative, in praise, with an implied «هو».

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَلَهُ الكبريآء فِي السماوات}: «في السماوات» may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الكبرياء», or attached to what the first adverbial phrase is attached to, since it occurs as khabar. It may also be attached to «الكبرياء» itself, since it is a maṣdar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "and it may be, meaning «في السماوات», an adverbial, with the operator in it being the first adverbial phrase and «الكِبْرياء», because it has the sense of grandeur." There is no need to interpret «الكبرياء» as having the sense of grandeur, for its being a maṣdar is established.

ukberi-tibyan:10-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مَا كَسَبُوا شَيْئًا وَلَا مَا اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٠) هَذَا هُدًى وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ (١١)).
His saying (وَلَا مَا اتَّخَذُوا): it is conjoined to «مَا كَسَبُوا», and «مَا» in both has the sense of الَّذِي (that which), or is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar).
And (مِنْ رِجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ) has been mentioned in Sabaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِنْهُ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١٣)).
His saying (جَمِيعًا مِنْهُ): «مِنْهُ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to سَخَّرَ, or be a naʿt (adjective) of جَمِيعًا.
It is also read مِنْهُ in the accusative [Translator's note: the text writes «مِنْهُ»; the reading meant is evidently مِنَّةً], i.e. [as a maṣdar of] bestowing favour (al-imtinān), or "He bestowed it upon you as a favour".
It is also read «مِنْهُ» in the nominative and as a construct (مَنُّهُ), as the fāʿil (agent) of «سَخَّرَ», or on the implied wording "that is His favour".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْمًا بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (١٤)).
His saying (قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا): its like has been mentioned in Ibrāhīm.
His saying (لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْمًا): with yāʾ and with nūn (لِنَجْزِيَ), in the active voice; and it is clear.
It is also read in the passive (لِيُجْزَى) with قَوْمًا in the accusative, and there are two views on that:
The first, and it is the good one: that the implied wording is "that the good may be given in requital to a people", on the view that the khabar [Translator's note: so in the text («الْخَبَرَ»); evidently «الْخَيْرَ», "the good", is meant] is originally a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as in your saying جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا ("may Allah requite you with good"); and making the second object stand in the place of the agent is permissible.
The second: that what stands in the place of the agent is the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "that the requital may be given"; and this is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ أَنْ نَجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَاءً مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ (٢١)).
His saying (سَوَاءً مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ): «سَوَاءً» is read in the nominative (سَوَاءٌ); so مَحْيَاهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), مَمَاتُهُمْ is conjoined to it, and سَوَاءٌ is a fronted khabar (predicate).
(سَوَاءً) is also read in the accusative, and there are two views on that. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the kāf, i.e. "We make them like the believers in this state".
The second: that it is the second object of حَسِبَ, with the kāf as a ḥāl; on this view the equality of their life and death is included in the reckoning.
And (مَحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ) are nominative by سَوَاءً, because it means "equal" (mustawin), and it has been read leaning on [what precedes].
It is also read (مَمَاتَهُمْ) in the accusative, i.e. "in their life and their death", governed by نَجْعَلَ or by سَوَاءً. It is also said: they are two adverbs of time. As for the pronoun in the genitive construct, it refers to both groups; it may also refer to the disbelievers, because their life is like their death; and for this reason the disbeliever is called dead.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَهَهُ هَوَاهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ وَخَتَمَ عَلَى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلَى بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٢٣)).
And (عَلَى عِلْمٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (مَنْ يَهْدِيهِ) is a question. (مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ): i.e. after Allah's leading him astray.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ (٢٧)).
His saying (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ): it is a badal (substitute) of the first «يَوْمَ».

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتَرَى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعَى إِلَى كِتَابِهَا الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying (كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تُدْعَى» is its khabar (predicate).
It was also read in the accusative (كُلَّ) as a badal (substitute) of the first كُلَّ; on this view تُدْعَى is a second object, or a naʿt (adjective) of كُلَّ, or of أُمَّةٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَذَا كِتَابُنَا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٩)).
His saying (يَنْطِقُ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِتَابِ, or a second khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا قُلْتُمْ مَا نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ (٣٢)).
His saying (وَالسَّاعَةُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا): it is read in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: it is conjoined to the position of «إِنَّ» and what it governs. It is also read in the accusative (وَالسَّاعَةَ), conjoined to the noun of «إِنَّ».
His saying (إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا): its implied wording is "we do nothing but suppose a supposing" (إِنْ نَحْنُ إِلَّا نَظُنُّ ظَنًّا); so إِلَّا is displaced to a later position; were it not for this implied wording, the meaning would be "we do not suppose except that we suppose". It is also said: it is in its proper place, because نَظُنُّ may have the sense of knowledge and of doubt; so He excepted doubt, i.e. "we have no belief except doubt".

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ).
His saying (فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْكِبْرِيَاءُ, governed by [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār); or an adverbial (ẓarf), governed by the first adverbial phrase or by الْكِبْرِيَاءُ, because it has the sense of "greatness".

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ آيَاتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ (٤) وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ رِزْقٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ آيَاتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٥)).
His saying (آيَاتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ): it is read with kasra on the tāʾ (آيَاتٍ), and there are two views on that:
The first: that «إِنَّ» is implied, omitted because the first إِنَّ indicates it; and «آيَاتٍ» is not conjoined to the first آيَاتٍ, because that would involve conjoining to [the objects of] two governors (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā ʿāmilayn).
The second: that «آيَاتٍ» is repeated for emphasis (tawkīd), since it is the same word as the first آيَاتٍ, and so it was given its case; as in your saying "There is blood on your garment, and on Zayd's garment blood" (إِنَّ بِثَوْبِكَ دَمًا، وَبِثَوْبِ زَيْدٍ دَمًا): the second دَمًا is a repetition, because you could do without mentioning it.
It is also read in the nominative (آيَاتٌ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «فِي خَلْقِكُمْ» as its khabar (predicate); and it is a resumptive clause.
It is also said: in the nominative too it is by way of emphasis.
As for His saying (وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ), it is genitive by an implied فِي other than the first.
And (آيَاتٌ) [in verse ٥] is with kasra and in the nominative, as explained above.
It is also possible that «اخْتِلَافِ» is conjoined to the noun made genitive by فِي, with «آيَاتٍ» as emphasis.
Some permitted that this be a case of conjoining to [the objects of] two governors.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ (٦)).
His saying (نَتْلُوهَا): its i'rab has been mentioned at His saying (نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ (٧) يَسْمَعُ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِرًا كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْهَا فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ (٨)).
His saying (يَسْمَعُ): it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «أَثِيمٍ», or resumptive.
And (تُتْلَى) is a ḥāl; and «كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْهَا» is also a ḥāl.

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ لَكم ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِنهُ﴾: It is also read "مِنَّةً" (as a favour). "جَمِيعًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning is: "All of that is from Him, as bounty and beneficence." "مِنَّةً" is with the meaning of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the meaning being: "He did that as a favour," that is, "He bestowed a favour," because His subjecting [them] has the meaning of "He bestowed favour upon you."

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿هَذا بَصائِرُ لِلنّاسِ وهُدًى ورَحْمَةٌ﴾: "هَذا" is a reference to the Qur'an; the meaning is: "This Qur'an is insights for mankind."

zajjaj:21-21.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئاتِ أنْ نَجْعَلَهم كالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ سَواءً مَحْياهم ومَماتُهُمْ﴾: It is also read "سَواءٌ مَحْياهم ومَماتُهم", and it has been read "سَواءٌ مَحْياهم ومَماتَهم", with "المَماتِ" in the accusative; some grammarians have reported that this is permissible in Arabic. The meaning of "اِجْتَرَحُوا" is: they earned; one says "فُلانٌ جارِحَةُ أهْلِهِ" (so-and-so is his family's jāriḥa), that is, their earner. The preferred [reading] according to Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans is "سَواءٌ", with "سَواءٌ" in the nominative, and most of the readers follow it; but they allow the accusative. You say: "ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا سَواءٌ أبُوهُ وأُمُّهُ" and "سَواءً أبُوهُ وأُمُّهُ" (I thought Zayd's father and mother alike), and the nominative is better, because "سَواءٌ" follows the pattern of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say: "ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا ذُو اسْتِواءٍ أبُوهُ وأُمُّهُ". Whoever reads "سَواءً" in the accusative puts it in the position of "مُسْتَوِيًا مَحْياهم ومَماتُهم" (their life and their death being equal). Whoever puts "مَحْياهم ومَماتَهم" in the accusative, it is, according to some grammarians, "equal in their life and in their death," treating it as [adverbs of] time. It is also permissible otherwise, by making it a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and mīm [of "نَجْعَلَهم"], the meaning being: "Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make their life and their death equal to those who believe and do righteous deeds," that is, to the life and death of those who believe and do righteous deeds.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
And His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إلَهَهُ هَواهُ وأضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾: It has been transmitted as "آلِهَتَهُ هَواهُ" (his gods), and that has a basis in the exegesis. It is reported that Quraysh used to worship al-ʿUzzā, which was a white stone; when they saw a stone whiter and finer than it, they would take that finer one and discard the first. This supports "آلِهَتَهُ", and likewise also "إلَهَهُ".
And His saying: ﴿وَأضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾: that is, in accordance with what preceded in His knowledge, before He created him, that he would be astray.
﴿وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً﴾: It is also read "غَشْوَةً", with fatḥa on the ghayn and without alif, and it is read "غُشاوَةً", with ḍamma on the ghayn and with the alif.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا ما هي إلا حَياتُنا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ ونَحْيا وما يُهْلِكُنا إلا الدَّهْرُ﴾.
If someone asks: How did they say "We die and we live," when they do not acknowledge the resurrection — the proof that they do not acknowledge the resurrection being their saying "There is nothing but our life"? [The answer is that] there are three views on "نَمُوتُ ونَحْيا". The meaning may be: "We die and we live," i.e. our children live, so some people die and some people live. Or the meaning of "نَمُوتُ ونَحْيا" may be "We live and we die," because the wāw is for combination and contains no indication that one of the two things comes before the other. Or "نَمُوتُ ونَحْيا وما يُهْلِكُنا إلّا الدَّهْرُ" may mean: our beginning is lifelessness in the origin of creation, then we live, then time destroys us. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they say that in error and doubt, and said: ﴿وَما لَهم بِذَلِكَ مِن عِلْمٍ إنْ هم إلا يَظُنُّونَ﴾; the meaning is: "They do nothing but conjecture."

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما كانَ حُجَّتَهم إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾: The nominative is permissible in "حُجَّتَهم". Whoever uses the nominative makes "حُجَّتَهم" the noun (ism) of "كانَ" and "أنْ قالُوا" the khabar (predicate) of "كانَ". Whoever uses the accusative for "حُجَّتَهم" makes the noun of "كانَ" "أنْ" together with its ṣila (relative clause), and the meaning is: "Their argument was nothing but their saying: Bring back our forefathers."

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى إلى كِتابِها﴾: that is, everyone will be requited according to what his record contains, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسانٍ ألْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ في عُنُقِهِ ونُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ كِتابًا يَلْقاهُ مَنشُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13] ﴿اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 14]; this is like His saying ﴿كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى إلى كِتابِها﴾. "كُلُّ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is "تُدْعى إلى كِتابِها". Whoever reads the accusative makes it a badal (substitute) for the first "كُلَّ", and the meaning is: "And you will see every nation called to its record." The meaning of "جاثِيَةً" is: sitting on the knees. One says: "قَدْ جَثا فُلانٌ، يَجْثُو" when he sits on his knee; and similar is "جَذا، يَجْذُو". "اَلْجُذُوُّ" is a more on-edge posture than "al-jathw", because al-jadhw is that one sits on the tips of his toes.

zajjaj:29-29.t: And His saying: ﴿إنّا كُنّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: "اَلِاسْتِنْساخُ" (transcription) can only be from an original; it is that one transcribes a book from a book. So "We transcribe" what the recording guardians (al-ḥafaẓa) write, and it is established with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
Sūrat al-Jāthiya
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ لآياتٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "In the creation of the heavens and the earth there are signs." This is indicated by His saying: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكم وما يَبُثُّ مِن دابَّةٍ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 4], which is read "آياتٍ" and "آياتٌ", with the tāʾ in the genitive (i.e. kasra) and in the nominative. [With kasra] it is in the position of the accusative by conjunction (nasaq) with His saying ﴿إنَّ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ لآياتٍ﴾, the meaning being: "In your creation there are signs." Whoever reads "لَآياتٌ", it is on two bases: as resumptive (istiʾnāf), with the meaning "And in your creation there are signs"; or [by conjunction] on the position of "إنَّ" together with what it governs. You say: "إنَّ زَيْدًا قائِمٌ وعَمْرًا" and "وعَمْرٌو": you conjoin "عَمْرًا" to "زَيْدٍ" when you use the accusative; and when you use the nominative, it is on the position of "إنَّ" together with "زَيْدٌ", since the meaning of "إنَّ زَيْدًا قائِمٌ" is "زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ" (Zayd is standing).

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: the answer (jawāb) of "أمّا" is omitted, because there is an indication of it in the speech. The meaning is: "And as for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them: Were not My verses recited to you?!" The fāʾ in His saying "أفَلَمْ" indicates the omitted fāʾ in your saying "فَيُقالُ لَهم" (then it will be said to them).

zajjaj:32-32.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ إنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ والسّاعَةُ لا رَيْبَ فِيها﴾, and "اَلسّاعَةَ" [is also read]. Whoever reads the accusative conjoins it to "الوَعْدِ" (the promise), the meaning being: "And when it was said: Allah's promise is true, and the Hour…". Whoever reads the nominative, it is with the meaning "and it was said: The Hour, there is no doubt about it."

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقِيلَ اليَوْمَ نَنْساكم كَما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكم هَذا ومَأْواكُمُ النّارُ﴾: that is, today We leave you in the punishment, just as you left faith and working for this day of yours. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿فاليَوْمَ لا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنها ولا هم يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 35]: they will not be sent back, and no deed or obedience will be sought from them.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ الكِبْرِياءُ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: that is, to Him belongs the majesty in the heavens and the earth.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying: ﴿واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ وما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِن رِزْقٍ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾: It is read in the nominative, and with kasra on the tāʾ and tanwīn, in which case the position is that of the accusative. His saying ﴿واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾ is then conjoined to His saying ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 4] and to His saying ﴿إنَّ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 3]: "and in the alternation of night and day there are signs (āyātin)." This is conjunction upon two governing words (ʿaṭf ʿalā ʿāmilayn). Its like in poetry:
أكُلَّ امْرِئٍ تَحْسَبِينَ امْرَأً ∗∗∗ ونارٍ تَوَقَّدُ بِاللَّيْلِ نارا
(Do you reckon every man a [true] man, and every fire that blazes by night a fire?)
He conjoined to what "كُلُّ" governs and to what "أتَحْسَبِينَ" governs. Some grammarians have rejected it and said: only the nominative is permissible in His saying ﴿وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ آياتٌ﴾, making it a conjunction upon a single governing word, with the meaning: "And the alternation of night and day and the turning of the winds are signs." But this too is conjunction upon two governing words, because he puts "آياتٌ" in the nominative by conjunction with what precedes it, just as he puts "واخْتِلافِ" in the genitive by conjunction with what precedes it. It may be conjoined, if you wish, to the position of "إنَّ" and what it governs, or, if you wish, according to the reading of whoever reads "وَفي خَلْقِكم وما يَبُثُّ مِن دابَّةٍ آياتٍ".

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبِأيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وآياتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, and "تُؤْمِنُونَ" — both [are read]. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "In what discourse, after the Book of Allah and His signs, will they believe?!" Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿اللَّهُ نَـزَّلَ أحْسَنَ الحَدِيثِ كِتابًا مُتَشابِهًا مَثانِيَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 23], thus making the Qur'an the best discourse.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ أفّاكٍ أثِيمٍ﴾: "أفّاكٍ" means a great liar.
